en: 4  The Invention and Reinvention of the Peasant
zh: 4  农民的发明与再发明

en: Among the figures in the scholarly imagining of the postcolonial world, “the peasant” is a strange kind of presence. With this abstraction a category of human being became a field of expertise, the subject of his own scholarly journals and the object of a distinct body of theory and description. “What are villagers in India, in Egypt, in Mexico really like?” the anthropologist George Foster asks, as he begins a brief history of the field.“For nearly fifty years anthropologists (by no means to the exclusion of others) have searched for answers [to this question] . . . living with villagers in order to question them and to observe their behavior, describing their findings in books and articles.” At first they called their research the study of “folk” societies, Foster says, but after World War II scholars “came to realize that ‘peasant’ is a more appropriate term, and thus was born the new subfield of ‘peasant studies.’ “
zh: 在学术对后殖民世界的想象所塑造的诸种形象中，“农民”是一种奇特的存在。借助这一抽象概念，一类人变成了一个专门知识领域，成为专属学术期刊的主题，也成为一套独特理论与描述的对象。“印度、埃及、墨西哥的村民实际上是什么样的人？”人类学家乔治·福斯特在开始简述该领域的历史时问道。“近五十年来，人类学家（绝非只有他们）一直在寻找［这个问题的］答案……他们与村民同住，以便询问村民并观察其行为，又在书籍和文章中描述自己的发现。”福斯特说，起初他们把自己的研究称为对“民俗”社会的研究，但第二次世界大战之后，学者们“逐渐认识到‘农民’是一个更恰当的说法，于是‘农民研究’这一新分支领域就此诞生。”

en: Foster makes these remarks in his foreword to the book Shahhat: An Egyptian, by Richard Critchfield, which he recommends for its accurate portrayal of what peasants everywhere are really like, and which became a favorite of both hotel bookstores in Cairo and college-level introductions to the Third World in the United States. The book belongs to a genre of peasant studies for which scholarship on the Middle East, more than other parts of the Third World, has provided an important home, a genre I would call descriptive realism. Critchfield sets before us the peasant’s life “like a series of wonderfully composed photographs,” wrote one of the book’s reviewers; “when taken together, they make us see and feel the contours and the substance of fellah culture.”

Despite the claims of photographic realism, however, a careful reading of Critchfield’s book reveals his “real peasant” to be something constructed out of earlier representations, as a collage of familiar Orientalist images juxtaposed with clippings taken—in fact plagiarized— from earlier writings, in particular from the previous popular study in a similar genre, The Egyptian Peasant by Henry Ayrout.
zh: 福斯特的这些话写在他为理查德·克里奇菲尔德的《沙哈特：一个埃及人》所作的序言中。他推荐此书，因为它准确描绘了各地农民的实际情况；这本书既成为开罗各旅馆书店的抢手货，也成为美国大学第三世界入门课程的常用读物。该书属于农民研究的一种体裁，而中东研究比其他第三世界地区为此类体裁提供了更重要的园地；我愿把这一体裁称为“描述性现实主义”。该书的一位评论者写道，克里奇菲尔德把农民的生活“像一组构图精美的照片”呈现在我们面前；“合在一起，它们使我们看到并感受到费拉欣文化的轮廓与实质。”
然而，尽管声称具有摄影般的写实性，细读克里奇菲尔德的书会发现，他的“真正的农民”是由早先的各种再现拼凑而成的东西，是熟悉的东方主义意象与取自早先著作的剪贴——实际上是抄袭——并置而成的拼贴画，尤其是取自同一体裁中先前那部流行的研究，亨利·艾鲁特的《埃及农民》。

en: This chapter examines the genealogy of Critchfield’s Egyptian peasant, not just to bring to light these forms of repetition and borrowing, but to ask some larger questions. What is the nature of this realist genre in peasant studies? Why is the Middle East, with its dearth of more critical examinations of rural society, so well represented? Why are the results so widely accepted, acquiring so easily the status of classics? Why does the realism of the peasant’s portrayal seem to require not only the borrowings from earlier writings but also the exclusion from the picture of history, of the West, and of the presence of the Western author? Overall, what political processes are at work in the producing and reproducing of all this realism?
zh: 本章考察克里奇菲尔德笔下埃及农民的谱系，不仅是为了揭示这些重复与借用，而且是为了提出一些更大的问题。农民研究中的这种现实主义体裁具有何种性质？中东对乡村社会较为批判性的考察如此稀少，为什么在此类体裁中却有如此充分的呈现？为什么这些成果被如此广泛接受，如此轻易地获得经典地位？为什么对农民的这种现实主义描绘似乎不仅需要借用早先的著作，而且需要把历史、西方以及西方作者本人的在场排除在画面之外？总体而言，在所有这些现实主义的制造与再生产中，有哪些政治过程在起作用？

en: The emergence of peasant studies as a new field of expertise more than half a century ago can be located quite precisely in the widespread rebellions that rural populations were able to organize against occupying European powers during the interwar years. In the Arab world, for example, rural uprisings in Egypt, Morocco, Syria, and Iraq in the years after World War I were followed by the Palestinian uprising of 1936–39, the first sustained anticolonial revolt, which required one-third of Britain’s armed forces to suppress it and a commission of colonial experts to examine rural life in Palestine and explain the rebellion’s causes. In Indochina, peasant uprisings during the early 1930s that succeeded in establishing selfgoverning soviets were the background to studies such as Pierre Gourou’s classic Les Paysans du delta tonkinois (1936), a work advising the colonial authorities of the “delicate” task they faced in preserving the existing Vietnamese “moral and social” system that it so meticulously described, along with the peasants’ “strikingly wretched material conditions.” The book warned that if the author’s words were ignored and this “traditional” world were allowed to collapse, the peasantry would then “have a clear picture of its poverty and would center its thoughts on it.”
As the rebellions spread, the experts kept up. The uprising in Palestine affected provincial Egypt, where political organizing and economic protest intensified in 1938 and 1939.

Several diagnoses of the peasant condition were put into print, including Ayrout’s famous study of the Egyptian peasant, first published in 1938 under the title Moeurs et coutumes des fellahs, which claimed to “photograph” for the first time “the realities of peasant life” among Egyptians—and which compared itself, in turn, to the work on Vietnam by Gourou.
zh: 半个多世纪以前，农民研究作为一个新的专门知识领域出现，其时间可以相当准确地定位于两次世界大战之间乡村人口为反抗欧洲占领国而能够组织起来的广泛起义。例如在阿拉伯世界，第一次世界大战后埃及、摩洛哥、叙利亚和伊拉克的乡村起义之后，是1936—1939年的巴勒斯坦起义——第一场持久性的反殖民叛乱；镇压它动用了英国三分之一的武装力量，并需要一个殖民专家委员会来考察巴勒斯坦的乡村生活、解释叛乱的原因。在印度支那，1930年代初成功建立自治苏维埃的农民起义，是皮埃尔·古鲁的经典著作《东京湾三角洲的农民》（Les Paysans du delta tonkinois，1936）等研究的背景。该书提醒殖民当局，他们在维持其细致描述的越南既有“道德与社会”体系方面面临着“微妙”的任务，同时还要面对农民“惊人的悲惨物质状况”。该书警告说，如果无视作者的话，任由这个“传统”世界崩溃，农民就会“清楚地看到自己的贫困，并把心思集中在这上面”。
随着叛乱蔓延，专家们也紧随其后。巴勒斯坦起义影响了外省的埃及，1938年和1939年那里的政治组织与经济抗议活动加剧。
若干对农民状况的诊断被付印，其中包括艾鲁特关于埃及农民的名著，该书1938年以《费拉欣的风俗与习惯》（Moeurs et coutumes des fellahs）为题首次出版，声称首次为埃及人“拍摄下”“农民生活的现实”，又自比于古鲁关于越南的著作。

en: The picture of what peasants are “really like” has a curious history, as the subsequent reissuing of these kinds of texts reflects. Gourou’s study was translated into English in 1955 by the Human Relations Area Files, and between the late 1960s and mid-1970s it became one of the most important sources for studies on peasant revolt in Vietnam.

Ayrout’s work, written in France where its Egyptian author was training to become a Jesuit priest, was translated into Arabic (1943) and English (1945), and then, following the shifting focus of foreign interest in Egypt, into Russian in 1954, and finally into English again in the United States in 1963.

By the early 1960s American scholarship was becoming increasingly interested in the question of peasant politics, urged on by events in Indochina and elsewhere and by figures such as undersecretary of state Chester Bowles, who as chairman of the Democratic Platform Committee in the 1960 elections had secured American commitment to a new economic policy toward the Third World.

Ayrout’s Egyptian Peasant was published with an introduction by the sociologist Morroe Berger of Princeton, at that time considered the senior American scholar of the contemporary Middle East. Berger noted, twenty-five years after the book’s first edition, that although political feelings in rural Egypt had still “hardly begun to develop,” the government of President Nasser was now seeking “to awaken ambition and expectation among the peasants.”

These observations were preceded by a foreword from Chester Bowles himself, warning that everywhere in Asia, Africa, and Latin America, “peasants are rousing themselves from apathy and despair to ask hard economic and political questions,” and that with the spread of “communist agitators” they now “constitute fertile ground for subversion and unrest.”
zh: 关于农民“实际上是什么样子”的图景有一段奇特的历史，这类文本后来的再版经历正反映了这一点。古鲁的研究于1955年由人类关系区域档案翻译成英文，并在1960年代末至1970年代中期成为研究越南农民起义的最重要资料来源之一。
艾鲁特的著作写于法国，当时这位埃及作者正在那里受训成为耶稣会神父；该书被译成阿拉伯文（1943）和英文（1945），随后随着外国对埃及兴趣焦点的转移，于1954年译成俄文，最后又于1963年在美国译成英文。
到1960年代初，美国的学术研究对农民政治问题越来越感兴趣；在印度支那等地的事件以及副国务卿切斯特·鲍尔斯等人物的推动下——鲍尔斯在1960年大选期间担任民主党纲领委员会主席时，曾促成美国承诺对第三世界实行一项新经济政策——这种兴趣不断增强。
艾鲁特的《埃及农民》出版时，附有普林斯顿大学社会学家莫罗·伯杰的导言；伯杰当时被认为是美国研究当代中东的资深学者。伯杰在本书第一版问世二十五年后指出，尽管埃及乡村的政治情绪仍然“几乎尚未发展起来”，纳赛尔总统的政府此时却正寻求“在农民中唤起雄心与期望”。
这些评论之前还有切斯特·鲍尔斯本人撰写的序言，他警告说，在亚洲、非洲和拉丁美洲各地，“农民正在从麻木与绝望中觉醒，提出尖锐的经济和政治问题”；随着“共产主义鼓动者”的扩散，他们现在“构成了颠覆与动乱的肥沃土壤”。

en: American interest in helping Nasser deal with rural agitation and unrest subsided in the mid-1960s, after the Egyptians failed to fit their domestic and foreign policy to America’s expanding regional interests. The need to expand American power reflected problems elsewhere in the world, in particular the intensification of the war against Vietnam. It is no coincidence that Vietnam was where Richard Critchfield first acquired his anthropological interest in peasant villages, while serving there from 1964 to 1967 as a reporter for the Washington Star. “What began as the reporting of events (conventional journalism),” he explained autobiographically, “ended in the study of the culture of ordinary people (amateur anthropology). It was that kind of war,” he added, echoing a generation later the sentiments of the French ethnographer Pierre Gourou: “by 1967 the restoration of traditional Vietnamese values was the only chance left of saving the country.”

Critchfield’s first book, The Long Charade: Political Subversion in the Vietnam War (1968), presented to American readers the views of British military advisors in South Vietnam, who represented a colonial expertise in dealing with rural “terrorism” accumulated earlier in Malaya and Palestine. The war in Vietnam, he explained with their help, was not a struggle for national liberation but a problem of “law and order.” The government’s police force had been weakened by terrorism in the countryside, and only by reestablishing “permanent security in the towns and villages” could “traditional” leaders and values be reestablished.
“The villagers were the key. But how to get to know them well enough to help them against the terrorism which was destroying their confidence and their culture,” Critchfield wrote.

After leaving Vietnam Critchfield went on to visit and write about villages in Indonesia, India, Mauritius, Iran, and finally Egypt, where he spent several months during the years 1974–75 getting to know the Upper Egyptian village that was to be the subject of Shahhat: An Egyptian, his first full-length village study.
zh: 美国帮助纳赛尔处理乡村骚动与动乱的兴趣，在1960年代中期减退，因为埃及人未能使其内外政策配合美国不断扩大的地区利益。扩展美国实力的需要反映了世界其他地方的问题，特别是对越战争的加剧。并非巧合，越南正是理查德·克里奇菲尔德最初获得对农民村庄的人类学兴趣的地方；1964年至1967年，他在那里担任《华盛顿星报》记者。“起初是报道事件（常规新闻工作），”他在自传性说明中解释道，“最终却成了对普通人文化的研究（业余人类学）。”他补充说，正是那种战争——隔了一代人之后，呼应了法国民族志学者皮埃尔·古鲁的感受——“到1967年，恢复越南传统价值观是拯救这个国家的最后机会。”
克里奇菲尔德的处女作《漫长的骗局：越南战争中的政治颠覆》（1968），向美国读者介绍了英国军事顾问在南越的观点；这些顾问代表了此前在马来亚和巴勒斯坦积累起来的、处理乡村“恐怖主义”的殖民专门知识。他借助这些顾问解释说，越南战争不是争取民族解放的斗争，而是“法律与秩序”问题。政府的警察力量已被乡间的恐怖主义削弱，只有重建“城镇与村庄的永久安全”，才能重新确立“传统”领袖与价值观。
“村民是关键。但怎样才能充分了解他们，帮助他们对抗正在摧毁其信心与文化的恐怖主义，”克里奇菲尔德写道。
离开越南后，克里奇菲尔德又走访并书写了印度尼西亚、印度、毛里求斯、伊朗的村庄，最后是埃及。1974至1975年间，他在埃及逗留数月，了解上埃及的一座村庄；这座村庄将成为《沙哈特：一个埃及人》的主题，那是他的第一部完整村庄研究。

en: The years 1974–75 marked the beginning of a new American interest in rural Egypt, as President Sadat abandoned his predecessor’s policies, aligned his foreign policy with the United States, and reopened the country to private capital investment. Shahhat was published in 1978, two months after Sadat’s journey to Jerusalem and at the height of his popularity in the United States. The chairman of the Democratic National Committee this time around had been Robert Strauss, who was now a Middle East advisor to the White House and the coordinator of Sadat’s visits to the United States, including the Camp David negotiations later that year with Israel. Although Shahhat failed to get a foreword from Strauss to match Ayrout’s foreword from Chester Bowles, the author’s introduction inadvertently locates the study of peasants in the context of U.S. interests in Egypt, including the interests of men like Robert Strauss. The introduction summarizes an interview the author obtained with Sadat, who is described as “Egypt’s first ruler of truly fellaheen origins” (in fact he was the son of a minor functionary employed by the British army in Egypt, and moved from the provinces to Cairo as a young child).

The president, we are told, “was deeply concerned about the disruptive effect of rapid change as raised in this story, especially in the villages,” and his plans for rural Egypt included switching to “highvalue cash crops” and “investing heavily in agri-industry.” Transferring farmland out of village control into large commercial hands coincided with the interests of American agribusiness corporations, including Coca-Cola and Pepsico, for whom Camp David confirmed the ending of the Egyptian boycott of American soft drink companies and the opening up of an important new market. Both companies embarked on investment projects in Egypt in the late 1970s, including a twenty-thousand-acre citrus-growing project to produce soft-drink concentrates negotiated jointly by Taha Zaki (an advisor to the Egyptian government on “food security”) and a director of Pepsico—the White House advisor Robert Strauss.
zh: 1974—1975年标志着美国对埃及乡村的新一轮兴趣的开端：萨达特总统抛弃前任的政策，使外交政策与美国保持一致，并重新向私人资本投资开放国家。《沙哈特》于1978年出版，即萨达特访问耶路撒冷两个月之后，也正值他在美国声望最高之际。这一次的民主党全国委员会主席是罗伯特·斯特劳斯；他此时已是白宫的中东顾问，也是萨达特访美行程的协调人，包括那年晚些时候与以色列的戴维营谈判。虽然《沙哈特》未能请到斯特劳斯作序，与艾鲁特请到切斯特·鲍尔斯作序相媲美，但作者的导言却无意中把农民研究置于美国在埃及利益的语境之中，包括像罗伯特·斯特劳斯这样的人的利益。导言概述了作者对萨达特的一次采访；萨达特被描述为“埃及第一位真正出身费拉欣的统治者”（事实上，他是一名受雇于驻埃英军的小官吏之子，幼年便从外省迁居开罗）。

据称，总统“对本故事所提出的迅速变化的破坏性影响深感关切，尤其是在村庄”；他关于埃及乡村的计划包括转向“高价值经济作物”以及“大举投资农产品加工业”。把农田从村庄控制下转入大型商业企业之手，正合美国农业综合企业的利益，包括可口可乐和百事可乐；对它们而言，戴维营确认了埃及对美国软饮料公司抵制的结束，以及一个重要新市场的开放。两家公司都在1970年代后期开始在埃及开展投资项目，其中包括一个两万费丹的柑橘种植项目，用于生产软饮料浓缩汁；该项目由塔哈·扎基（埃及政府“粮食安全”顾问）与百事公司的一位董事——白宫顾问罗伯特·斯特劳斯——共同谈成。

en: It was in this new period of renewed American interest in the economy and society of Egypt that Critchfield published his account of what rural Egyptians are really like. As with “any story set in the Third World today, particularly the Arab world,” we are warned, the book deals with the difficult ground of “cultural and psychological turbulence.” Shahhat, the rather petulant adolescent who is the story’s central character, is said to be in many ways “typical of the great mass of poor Egyptians,” and since his fellow villagers “all represent people found in the Third World today,” the author tells us that he “found Shahhat and his problems exemplary.” The problems involved are those that face a violence-prone adolescent as he adjusts to the recent death of his weak and alcoholic father amid the demands of an adoring and overbearing mother (as Robert Fernea remarks in his review of the book, “Freudian constructs haunt the scene”).

Presented as “the story of how a deeply traditional Egyptian, when faced with sudden changes in his way of life . . . comes of age,” Shahhat’s life is to be read as an individual enactment of the larger drama of “modernization,” in which villagers who have “never changed their way of life” in more than six thousand years are forced to adjust to modernity in less than a decade.
zh: 正是在美国重新燃起对埃及经济与社会兴趣的这一新时期，克里奇菲尔德出版了他关于埃及农民实际上是什么样子的记述。书前告诫读者，正如“当今任何以第三世界——尤其是阿拉伯世界——为背景的故事”一样，本书涉及“文化与心理动荡”这一艰难领域。故事的主人公沙哈特是个相当任性的少年，据说他在许多方面“典型地代表了广大贫困埃及人”；由于他的村邻“都代表了当今第三世界可见的人物”，作者告诉我们，他“觉得沙哈特及其问题具有典型意义”。这些问题是一个易于诉诸暴力的少年所面对的：他要在一位溺爱而专横的母亲的种种要求之间，适应软弱、酗酒的父亲新近去世（正如罗伯特·费尼亚在书评中所说，“弗洛伊德式构造在场景中萦绕”）。
本书被呈现为“一个深受传统束缚的埃及人在面对生活方式骤然变化时……长大成人的故事”，沙哈特的生活应被读作“现代化”这一更大戏剧的个体搬演：在这场戏剧中，六千多年来“从未改变生活方式”的村民被迫在不到十年里适应现代性。

en: The notion of a village life unchanged in sixty centuries is, of course, a complete fiction. To take just the nineteenth century, this region of Upper Egypt had seen the decline and virtual elimination of long-distance trade with India, Arabia, and the Sudan, the collapse of the local textile industry, and the introduction and spread of private landowning, export crops, steam-driven irrigation pumps, and epidemic diseases such as cholera. Large commercial estates were established, including the “feudal” estate to which Shahhat’s village belonged up until the 1952 revolution, which became a sugarcane plantation supplying the Egyptian Sugar Company. European armies arrived—the village of Qurna, adjacent to Shahhat’s village, was long remembered locally for its inhabitants’ armed resistance to the French soldiers of Napoleon

—and villagers themselves were conscripted for the first time into a modern Egyptian army and forced to pay the taxes to support it. In 1822–23, artisans and peasants in the region rebelled against conscription, taxation, and the destruction of local textile manufacturing, gathered a force of several hundred armed men, and established their headquarters in Shahhat’s village of Buʿairat. They marched on the local garrison and sacked it, causing the rebellion to spread throughout the surrounding countryside. The government dispatched European-officered reinforcements who burnt Buʿairat to the ground and rounded up and massacred the insurgents.

Police stations and telegraph lines were later built, and steamships and railways came, carrying government inspectors, European engineers, and great quantities of tourists and archaeologists, many of whom encamped in or near Shahhat’s village, which lies at the foot of the Theban necropolis, burial place of King Tut, perhaps the most famous archaeological and tourist site in the world. It is this place that Critchfield introduces to us as an untouched and therefore typical corner of the Third World, a hamlet “so obscure it barely has a name” (xxv).
zh: 村庄生活六千年不变这一观念，当然完全是虚构。仅以19世纪为例，上埃及的这一地区就经历了与印度、阿拉伯半岛和苏丹的长途贸易的衰落和几近消失，当地纺织业的崩溃，以及私有土地所有制、出口作物、蒸汽抽水机和霍乱等流行病的传入与扩散。大型商业庄园得以建立，包括沙哈特的村庄在1952年革命前一直所属的那座“封建”庄园；它变成了向埃及糖业公司供应原料的甘蔗种植园。欧洲军队到来——与沙哈特村庄相邻的古尔纳村，因当地居民对拿破仑法国士兵的武装抵抗而长期为当地人所铭记
——村民自己也首次被征入现代埃及军队，并被强迫纳税以供养军队。1822—1823年，该地区的手工匠人和农民反抗征兵、纳税以及当地纺织制造业遭到的破坏，聚集了数百名武装人员，把总部设在沙哈特的村庄布艾拉特。他们向当地驻军进军并将其洗劫一空，致使叛乱蔓延到周围乡村。政府派出由欧洲军官指挥的增援部队，将布艾拉特焚为平地，围捕并屠杀了起义者。
后来建起了警察局和电报线路，汽船和铁路也来了，载来政府视察员、欧洲工程师以及大量游客和考古学家，其中许多人就在沙哈特村庄之内或附近安营。该村位于底比斯墓地脚下——图坦卡蒙王的葬地，也许是世界上最著名的考古遗址和旅游胜地。克里奇菲尔德正是把这个地方介绍给我们，说它是第三世界一个未受触动、因而具有典型性的角落，一个“默默无闻得几乎没有名字”的小村（xxv）。

en: This blindness to historical transformation is carefully achieved. The essence of Critchfield’s method is to assure us at frequent intervals that everything we encounter in rural Egypt we have somehow seen before, in some exotic image from the past. Egyptian peasants are familiar in advance to those who have visited museum exhibits of ancient Egypt. Shahhat’s mother, for example, is immediately recognizable, for she has “the peculiarly straight nose, oval face, fair complexion, and large lustrous eyes familiar from ancient Egyptian statues and paintings” (4). In fact throughout Upper Egypt, we are told, “the facial and physical appearance of the villagers” resembles that of “the hundreds of statues and busts in the Cairo Museum” (xv). Then there are the inevitable echoes of the Bible. When Shahhat rescues a blonde female tourist from the cliff above the village, angrily chasing off some village boys who were following her, we are told that Shahhat, “in his black robes against the blindingly white rocks with the open blue sky all about, seemed very much a wrathful Old Testament figure” (111). We also get a quotation from the Rubayyat of Omar Khayyam (195), and several reminders of the Thousand and One Nights. A villager named Mitri, we are told,“resembled an old gnome out of Arabian Nights” (101) and even the infamous Habu Hotel, built in the village about a decade before as a hangout for the younger kind of European tourist, has “a medieval Arabian Nights air” (138).

Everything is encountered, it seems, as the original of something ancient and exotic that one has already seen in a museum, or read about in the literature of Orientalism, or imagined from the distant past.
zh: 这种对历史变迁的视而不见是精心造成的。克里奇菲尔德方法的核心，是每隔一段时间就向我们保证：我们在埃及乡村遇到的一切，都以某种方式在某种来自过去的异域意象中见过。对于看过古埃及博物馆展览的人，埃及农民是预先熟悉的。例如，沙哈特的母亲一眼就能辨认出来，因为她有“从古埃及雕像和绘画中熟悉的、特别挺直的鼻子、椭圆脸、白皙肤色和明亮的大眼睛”（4）。事实上，据说在整个上埃及，“村民的面容和身体外貌”都像“开罗博物馆里数百尊雕像和胸像”（xv）。接着还有不可避免的《圣经》回声。当沙哈特从村子上方的悬崖上救下一名金发女游客，愤怒地赶走几个尾随她的村中男孩时，据说沙哈特“身穿黑袍，映衬着令人目眩的白色岩石，四周是无际的蓝天，看上去很像一位愤怒的《旧约》人物”（111）。我们还读到一句欧玛尔·海亚姆《鲁拜集》的引文（195），以及几处对《一千零一夜》的提点。据说一位名叫米特里的村民“像《阿拉伯之夜》里走出来的老侏儒”（101）；甚至那座声名不佳的哈布旅馆——大约十年前为吸引较年轻的欧洲游客而在村中修建——也有“一种中世纪《阿拉伯之夜》的气息”（138）。
看来，一切都仿佛是作为某件古老而异域之物的“原件”被遭遇的，而那件东西人们早已在博物馆里见过、在东方主义文献中读过，或从遥远过去中想象过。

en: But Critchfield’s most important means of making peasant life seem something exotic and thus unchangingly familiar is his reliance on more recent writings, in particular the 1938 work of Henry Ayrout. He paraphrases The Egyptian Peasant from the opening pages. “Foreign conquerors have come and gone—the Persians, Greeks, Romans, Byzantines, Arabs, Turks, French and English. As Henry Habib Ayrout once observed, while the Upper Egyptian villagers changed their masters and their religion, their language and their crops, they never changed their way of life” (xiii).
Even Shahhat’s village of Buʿairat, where Critchfield stayed, is seen through Ayrout’s eyes.

The Egyptian village, wrote Ayrout, “forms a closed system . . . [of] habits, customs and taboos handed down from the distant past” (106). Forty years later Critchfield discovers that Shahhat’s village “was in fact a closed system,” which “preserved habits, customs, and taboos handed down from pharaonic times” (89). The peasant, Ayrout explained in his most famous line, “preserves and repeats, but does not originate anything” (132). Egyptian peasants, Critchfield unselfconsciously reiterates, “preserved and repeated, but did not originate, create, or change” (xvi).
zh: 但克里奇菲尔德使农民生活显得异域、从而显得始终如一的熟悉的更重要手段，是他依赖晚近的著作，尤其是亨利·艾鲁特1938年的作品。他从开篇几页起就改写《埃及农民》。“外国征服者来了又走——波斯人、希腊人、罗马人、拜占庭人、阿拉伯人、土耳其人、法国人和英国人。正如亨利·哈比卜·艾鲁特曾指出的，上埃及村民更换了主人，更换了宗教、语言和作物，却从未改变自己的生活方式”（xiii）。
甚至克里奇菲尔德逗留的沙哈特所在村庄布艾拉特，也是透过艾鲁特的眼睛来看的。
艾鲁特写道，埃及村庄“构成一个封闭系统……［由］从遥远过去传下来的习惯、风俗和禁忌”组成（106）。四十年后，克里奇菲尔德发现沙哈特的村庄“实际上是一个封闭系统”，它“保存着法老时代传下来的习惯、风俗和禁忌”（89）。艾鲁特在其最著名的一句话中解释说，农民“保存并重复，但不创造任何东西”（132）。克里奇菲尔德不自觉地重复道，埃及农民“保存并重复，但不发起、不创造、不改变”（xvi）。

en: Thus Critchfield’s village turns out to be the exotic kind of place we have somehow always visited before, in museums, Arabian nights, and guidebooks, but above all in studies of the Egyptian peasant. As we will see, the extent of this familiarity is quite astonishing in Critchfield’s case. Yet he is not the first to present rural Egypt as a living museum, familiar to us in advance through countless earlier texts and images. If one turns back to Ayrout, one encounters a similar problem. Rural Egyptians, Ayrout tells us in his first chapter (entitled “Changelessness”), are “as impervious and enduring as the granite of their temples, and as slow to develop.” The images one has of their daily life, whether from “Pharaonic tombs or from Coptic legend, from Arab historians or the Description of Egypt, from early English researchers or the travellers of our own day, seem to form a single sequence. . . . These scenes, though separated by so many centuries, only repeat and confirm one another” (20). The American edition of Ayrout adds that urban Egyptians who know nothing of the countryside and find it inaccessible by private car can now visit instead an agricultural museum in Cairo, which has been built “to introduce them to village life.”

Like Critchfield, however, Ayrout also reads rural Egypt through the pages of a more popular text, in this case the work of the turn-of-the-century French social psychologist Gustave Le Bon. Before continuing with my reading of Critchfield and showing the extent of his dependence on Ayrout, I will examine Ayrout’s own dependence on the work of Le Bon and explore how this dependence helped establish Ayrout’s book as the classic study of the Egyptian peasant.
zh: 于是，克里奇菲尔德的村庄变成了那种我们不知何故总是一再造访的异域地方——在博物馆、阿拉伯之夜和旅行指南中，但首先是在埃及农民研究之中。我们将会看到，在克里奇菲尔德的例子中，这种熟悉的程度相当惊人。然而，他并不是第一个把埃及乡村呈现为一座活人博物馆的人；通过无数早先的文本与图像，那里早已为我们所熟悉。回头去看艾鲁特，也会遇到类似的问题。艾鲁特在第一章（题为“不变”）中告诉我们，埃及乡村居民“像他们神庙的花岗岩一样不受侵蚀、历久长存，发展也同样缓慢”。人们关于他们日常生活的各种形象，无论来自“法老陵墓还是科普特传说，来自阿拉伯历史学家还是《埃及记述》，来自早期英国研究者还是我们同时代的旅行者，似乎都构成一个单一序列……这些场景虽相隔如此多世纪，却只是彼此重复、彼此印证”（20）。艾鲁特的美国版补充说，那些对乡村一无所知、又觉得乘私人汽车难以抵达的埃及城市居民，如今可以改去参观开罗的一座农业博物馆；该馆的建立就是为了“向他们介绍乡村生活”。
然而，和克里奇菲尔德一样，艾鲁特也通过一部更通俗的文本——即世纪之交法国社会心理学家古斯塔夫·勒邦的著作——来阅读埃及乡村。在继续解读克里奇菲尔德并展示他对艾鲁特依赖之深以前，我将先考察艾鲁特本人对勒邦著作的依赖，并探讨这种依赖如何帮助艾鲁特的书成为关于埃及农民的经典研究。

en: Le Bon’s writings, including Les lois psychologiques de l’évolution des peuples and his famous work Psychologie des foules (The Crowd), both of which were translated into Arabic and widely read in Cairo, were addressed to two pressing political questions of his day: how to explain scientifically the difference between advanced and backward societies, and how to explain scientifically the difference within a society between the mass of its people and the elite.

To account for these differences Le Bon introduced the concept of a people’s psyche or soul, a “collective mind” that consists of ideas, feelings, and beliefs and is created by a process of slow, hereditary accumulation. This accumulation, claimed Le Bon, which is the measure of a people’s evolution, occurs not among the mass of a nation but largely among its elite. Between the masses in a country such as Egypt, therefore, and those in parts of Europe, the difference in level of development might be small.“What most differentiates Europeans from Orientals is that only the former possess an élite of superior men.” It is this elite that “constitutes the true incarnation of the forces of a race.”

In his work on the crowd, described by Gordon Allport as “possibly the most influential book ever written in social psychology,” Le Bon employed the same principle to explain social differences within a society.

The crowd or mass (la foule), he explained, is composed of cells so merged together that they constitute a “provisional being,” with an unconscious collective mind. In this merger individual mental differences, the source—as he had shown—of all excellence, are lost. The loss of individuality, Le Bon concluded, makes the crowd into a less intelligent being, like a child, or like a backward nation or race. The backward nation and the crowd represent parallel states of mental inferiority, both caused by the absence of individuality.
zh: 勒邦的著作，包括《各民族进化中的心理规律》及其名著《乌合之众》（Psychologie des foules），都被译成阿拉伯文并在开罗被广泛阅读；这些著作回应了他那个时代的两个紧迫政治问题：如何科学地解释先进社会与落后社会之间的差异，以及如何科学地解释一个社会内部民众与精英之间的差异。

为解释这些差异，勒邦引入了民族心理或灵魂的概念，一种由观念、情感和信念构成、并通过缓慢的遗传积累过程形成的“集体心智”。勒邦声称，这种积累是衡量一个民族进化程度的尺度，它不是发生在民族的大众之中，而主要发生在其精英之中。因此，像埃及这样的国家的群众，与欧洲部分地区的群众之间，发展水平上的差异可能很小。“欧洲人与东方人最大的区别在于，只有前者拥有由优秀人物组成的精英。”正是这种精英“构成一个种族力量的真正化身”。
在其论群体的著作中——戈登·奥尔波特称该书“也许是社会心理学有史以来最有影响的著作”——勒邦运用同样的原则来解释一个社会内部的社会差异。
他解释说，群体或大众（la foule）由彼此融合得如此之深的细胞组成，以致构成一个“临时存在物”，拥有无意识的集体心智。在这种融合中，个体的心智差异——如他先前所表明的，这是一切卓越的源泉——消失了。勒邦的结论是，个体性的丧失使群体成为一个智力较低的存在物，像儿童，或像落后的民族或种族。落后民族与群体代表着两种平行的智力低劣状态，二者都由个体性的缺失造成。

en: Henry Ayrout adopted the vocabulary and thinking of Le Bon to explain the nature of the Egyptian peasant. “The fellah should always be spoken of in the plural,” he wrote, “because he lives always as a member of a group, if not of a crowd” (94).The peasant “is like a primitive man or child” (134), he explained, for like the primitive or the child he has “little individuality.” This is reflected in the “formlessness” of his village (116), where “all is dust and disorder. There is no plan or system, and not a single straight line” (100).

The lack of form and structure indicates the absence of individuality because without straight lines one cannot have individual houses. Like their occupants, the buildings are not separate units but are merged together and indistinguishable from one another, like cells “in the agricultural hive” (116).The absence of individual houses reflects, in turn, the absence of distinct families. The family, too, has no individual identity but simply “shades off into a wider community more or less closely interrelated by blood and marriage . . . . Just as the house is not a complete unit by itself, neither is the family which lives in it. As there is no real ‘home’ . . . so there is no real ‘family’ “ (125). Individuality and structure are also missing at the level of the village: “nothing is more like one Egyptian village than another Egyptian village. Here is another example of the monotonous uniformity” (95). The village itself, it follows, “is not a community in the social sense, not an organism, but a mass [une foule].” And, finally, at the level of the peasantry as a whole and of the nation:“One might well talk of Egypt in the plural. There is no single Egyptian people . . . but only a seething assemblage of the most varied types. . . . Neither is there a true peasant community, but only a homogeneous mass [une foule homogène]” (33).
zh: 亨利·艾鲁特采用勒邦的词汇和思想来解释埃及农民的本性。“谈论费拉赫时总该用复数，”他写道，“因为他始终作为群体的一员而生活，如果说不是作为人群的一员”（94）。他解释说，农民“像原始人或孩子”（134），因为像原始人或孩子一样，他“几乎没有个性”。这反映在他村庄的“无形式”上（116）：“一切都蒙着尘土、杂乱无章。没有规划或体系，也没有一条笔直的线”（100）。

形式与结构的缺失表明个体性的缺失，因为没有直线就不可能有独立的房屋。房屋像其中的居民一样，不是彼此分离的单元，而是融合在一起、彼此难以区分，如同“农业蜂巢”中的蜂房（116）。独立房屋的缺失又反映了独立家庭的缺失。家庭也没有个体身份，而只是“渐渐淡入一个更大的共同体，后者由血缘和婚姻或多或少紧密地联系在一起……正如房屋本身不是一个完整的单元，住在其中的家庭也不是。既然没有真正的‘家’……也就没有真正的‘家庭’”（125）。在村庄层面，个体性与结构同样缺失：“没有什么比一个埃及村庄更像另一个埃及村庄。这是单调一律的又一例证”（95）。由此可见，村庄本身“不是社会意义上的共同体，不是一个有机体，而是一群人［une foule］”。最后，在整个农民阶层和民族层面：“人们完全可以用复数来谈论埃及。并不存在一个单一的埃及民族……只有最纷繁多样的类型所构成的一锅沸腾的集合体。……也不存在真正的农民共同体，只有同质的人群［une foule homogène］”（33）。

en: All these absences in turn reflect a more fundamental absence, the lack of individual mental life, or what Ayrout, following Le Bon, calls “personality.” The peasant is “as little of a personality as he is of an individual,” Ayrout explains (110). The development of his intelligence, it seems, has “atrophied,” and what there is of it “is collective rather than personal.” He does not engage in “individual thinking.” Several “essential features” of the Egyptian mentality follow from this situation. The peasant is habitually distrustful and therefore selfish, “cunning to the point of duplicity,” fond of a “semi-conscious” state of torpor, and yet violent in the extreme when roused. His sense of justice is corrupt, and he lacks frankness, curiosity, ambition, sensibility, and initiative (132–38). How to account for these monstrous mental absences? “Some sociologists put it down to masturbation, which is fairly common in the Islamic East.” But according to Father Ayrout, that particular vice seems to be more common in urban areas, whereas these personality problems are more pronounced in the countryside (132). He explains them instead in terms of the miserable condition of rural life, though the “real evils” are not the poverty and hardship itself but the peasant’s “lack of education and culture,” as a result of which “he does not feel the depth of his suffering” (154), as well as the indifference of those who might help him, who have failed to notice “the distress which he himself could not put into words, and perhaps only half felt” (15).
zh: 所有这些缺失又反映了一种更根本的缺失，即个体精神生活的缺失，或者用艾鲁特追随勒邦的说法，即“人格”的缺失。艾鲁特解释说，农民“作为个体微不足道，作为人格同样微不足道”（110）。他的智力的发展似乎已经“萎缩”，而仅存的一点也“是集体的而非个人的”。他不进行“个体思考”。埃及人心性的若干“基本特征”由此而来。农民习惯性地不信任他人，因而自私，“狡黠到口是心非的程度”，喜欢“半意识”的麻木状态，可是一旦被激怒又极端暴烈。他的正义感是败坏的，并且缺乏坦率、好奇心、抱负、感受力和主动性（132—138）。如何解释这些惊人的精神缺失？“有些社会学家把它归咎于手淫，这在伊斯兰东方相当普遍。”但据艾鲁特神父说，那种恶习似乎在城市地区更常见，而这些人格问题在乡村却更为显著（132）。他转而用乡村生活的悲惨处境来解释这些问题，尽管“真正的祸害”不是贫困与艰辛本身，而是农民“缺乏教育和文化”，因此“他感受不到自己苦难的深度”（154）；同时也归因于那些本可帮助他的人的冷漠——这些人未能注意到“他自己无法言说、也许只感受到一半的痛苦”（15）。

en: The solution Ayrout suggests for this problem of an assemblage sans architecture, matériellement et intellectuellement, as the French original puts it, is a material and mental “reconstruction of the Egyptian village.”

He supports the various proposals being put forward in the 1930s and 1940s to replace the villages of Egypt with geometrical “model villages” of the sort already built on many of the country’s large commercial estates (his father was a well-known Cairo architect),
combined with a program of rural education (to which he devoted his own later life) that would provide villagers with the mental architecture needed to cope with straight lines and separate houses.

Such a program, Ayrout argues, is the responsibility of the Egyptian elite, or more specifically of a group he names the “rural middle class,” men like the nationalist leaders Saʿd Zaghlul and Mustafa Nahhas, “conservative, gain-loving, unpretentious” types who “live in the country and keep a close eye on the yield of their feddans.”This class is to be distinguished from the very largest landowners, who live only in the city and, like their allies the British and the European-owned credit companies and agricultural processing industries, are opposed to rural reform.
zh: 对于法文原著所说的这种在物质上和精神上都 sans architecture（无建筑结构）的集合体，艾鲁特提出的解决办法是对埃及村庄进行物质和精神上的“重建”。
他支持1930年代和1940年代提出的各种方案：用几何式的“模范村庄”取代埃及的村庄——这类村庄已在该国许多大型商业庄园中建成（他的父亲是一位著名的开罗建筑师）
——并配合一项乡村教育计划（他本人晚年即致力于此），向村民提供应付直线和独立房屋所需的精神建筑。
艾鲁特论证说，这样的计划是埃及精英的责任，更确切地说，是他称之为“乡村中产阶级”的那一群人的责任；这些人包括民族主义领袖萨阿德·扎格卢勒和穆斯塔法·纳哈斯，属于“保守、贪利、不事张扬”的类型，他们“住在乡下，密切关注自家费丹的收成”。这个阶级有别于最大的地主，后者只住在城里，并与其盟友英国人以及欧洲人拥有的信贷公司和农产品加工企业一样，反对乡村改革。

en: As these proposals make clear, Ayrout’s work forms a part of the political debate emerging in the late 1930s and 1940s, mentioned above in chapter 1, in which an educated Cairene elite began to see the rural population as a social problem. In 1938 alone, for example, the year Ayrout’s book was published, there appeared Mirrit Butrus Ghali’s Siyasat al-ghad (Policy of Tomorrow) and Hafiz Afifi’s ʿAla hamish al-siyasa (Notes on Politics), each of which includes an analysis, in different terms, of the situation of the rural population.

Ayrout’s contribution to this debate, in the familiar vocabulary of Le Bon, is to demonstrate how the peasantry lacks the ability even to feel their own suffering, and therefore requires the political intervention, as Le Bon had always stressed, of the nationalist elite, whose role is to “revive” the rural population, and yet, indicating the political dangers involved, to “awaken without exciting” (158–59).The duty of the elite, explains Ayrout, is “to liberate the fellah’s spirit from its stifling envelope of mud. . . . The initiative can never come from his own community, which is completely numbed and powerless, but only from the classes which overshadow him, from the élite, who with their riches of mind and money can vitalize him. In this dough must work the leaven of intelligence and sympathy” (23).
zh: 正如这些提议所表明的，艾鲁特的著作构成了1930年代末和1940年代出现的政治辩论的一部分——第一章已经提到过这场辩论——在这场辩论中，受过教育的开罗精英开始把乡村人口视为一个社会问题。例如，仅1938年，即艾鲁特的书出版那年，就出现了米尔里特·布特鲁斯·加利的《明日政策》（Siyasat al-ghad）和哈菲兹·阿菲菲的《政治边注》（ʿAla hamish al-siyasa），二者都以不同的措辞分析乡村人口的处境。

艾鲁特以勒邦那套熟悉的词汇参与这场辩论，其贡献在于说明农民甚至缺乏感受自身苦难的能力，因此需要民族主义精英进行政治干预——如勒邦一直强调的那样；后者的角色是“复兴”乡村人口，同时又要表明其中的政治危险，“唤醒而不激怒”（158—159）。艾鲁特解释说，精英的责任是“把费拉赫的精神从其令人窒息的泥浆外壳中解放出来……主动性永远不可能来自他自己的共同体，那个共同体完全麻木无力，而只能来自荫庇他的阶级，来自精英；精英以其心智和金钱的财富，能够赋予他活力。这团面团中必须揉入才智与同情的酵母”（23）。

en: This is the complex genealogy of the work that was to reappear in the United States in 1963, described on its cover by the dean of British and American Orientalists, Hamilton A. R. Gibb, as “a classic in its field.”

By what process had The Egyptian Peasant become a classic? First, there was what the American Sociological Review called “its continued relevance and its virtual monopoly of the subject”—twenty-five years after the first edition. The book was not the only study of the Egyptian peasant, as we have just seen—indeed if there were any classics they were Ibrahim ʿAmir’s al-Ard wa-ʾl-fallah (The Land and the Peasant, 1958), which influenced a generation of Egyptian scholars, and the writings of the French scholar Jacques Berque, but none of this work was translated into English.

Ayrout’s book had acquired its continued relevance and hence monopoly in the minds of Western scholars by its ahistorical method of explanation, in which the condition of rural Egypt is attributed not to political and economic forces of the day but to a timeless peasant mentality.

Morroe Berger, the senior American social scientist who wrote the introduction to the U.S. edition, had used this account of the peasant mind as a source for his own study, The Arab World Today (1962), generalizing Ayrout’s views to help answer the question, “what kind of person is the Arab?” Berger was able to report that “The Arab seems to harbor two major contradictory impulses,” combining “extreme self-assertion” with “an inability to assert independence as an individual,” not to mention his “virtual obsession with oral functions.” Prejudices of this sort, to which Ayrout’s milder stereotyping could lend authority, were not considered abnormal. To the contrary, Berger was at that time the chair of the Near and Middle East Committee of the Social Science Research Council and three years later became the founding president of the Middle East Studies Association of North America.
zh: 这就是这部著作复杂的谱系；它将于1963年在美国重新出现，封面上有英美东方学界泰斗汉密尔顿·A. R. 吉布的评语，称其为“该领域的经典”。

《埃及农民》是通过什么过程成为经典的？首先，是《美国社会学评论》所称的“其持续的相关性及其对这一主题的近乎垄断”——此时距第一版已二十五年。这本书并不是关于埃及农民的唯一研究，正如我们刚刚所见——事实上，如果说有什么经典的话，那应该是易卜拉欣·阿米尔的《土地与农民》（al-Ard wa-ʾl-fallah，1958）和法国学者雅克·贝尔克的著作；前者影响了一代埃及学者，但这些作品都没有被译成英文。
艾鲁特的书之所以在西方学者心中获得持续的相关性并因而独占该主题，靠的是其非历史的解释方法：它把埃及乡村的状况归因于一种永恒不变的农民心态，而不是当时的政治和经济力量。

为美国版撰写导言的美国资深社会科学家莫罗·伯杰，曾把这种关于农民心智的论述用作他自己研究《今日阿拉伯世界》（1962）的资料，把艾鲁特的观点加以概括，以帮助回答“阿拉伯人是什么样的人”这一问题。伯杰得以报告说，“阿拉伯人似乎怀有两种主要的矛盾冲动”，兼有“极端的自我主张”和“无法作为个体坚持独立”，更不用说其“对口腔功能的近乎执念”。诸如此类的偏见——艾鲁特较温和的刻板印象为之提供了权威——当时并不被视为异常。相反，伯杰当时是社会科学研究理事会近东与中东委员会主席，三年后成为北美中东研究协会的创会主席。

en: Then there was Ayrout’s realism. H. A. R. Gibb claimed that the book “holds up a mirror to the peasantry as they are.” A mirror was the correct metaphor, but, as we saw, it was a mirror reflecting not some original peasant reality but a series of other mirrors, ranging from the French Description d’Egypte and the writings of nineteenth-century European travelers to the exhibits in the Egyptian museum and, above all, the work of Gustave Le Bon. Such a system of mirrors produced an image of the peasantry appropriate to the writer’s political concerns and pastoral sympathies. But their overall effect was to make the book appear to confirm everything Orientalism had always suspected concerning the mentality and way of life of the Arab, thus guaranteeing its reception as a classic. It was no accident, furthermore, that Father Ayrout had been educated in France and wrote his study in French as a dissertation for a French university. Unlike works in Arabic, it was readily available for translation into British, Russian, and American editions. The final mechanisms for rendering the book a classic were the requirements of postwar American politics, in particular the complex of development programs and university Middle East courses. The English edition of 1945 was made available in the United States through the Human Relations Area Files, and apparently an initial American translation was produced by the U.S. Point Four program, presumably as an introduction to rural Egypt for American development experts.
“There is no better book,” the Economist remarked confidently when the Beacon Press edition finally appeared in 1963, “on the magnitude of President Nasser’s domestic task in rural Egypt.”
zh: 其次是艾鲁特的现实主义。H. A. R. 吉布声称，这本书“像一面镜子，照出农民的本相”。镜子是恰当的比喻，但正如我们所见，这面镜子所反射的并非某种原初的农民现实，而是一系列其他的镜子：从法国的《埃及记述》和19世纪欧洲旅行者的著作，到埃及博物馆的展品，而首先是古斯塔夫·勒邦的作品。这一镜子的系统所产生的农民形象，符合作者的政治关切和田园式同情。但它们的总体效果，是使这本书似乎印证了东方学关于阿拉伯人心性与生活方式一直猜测的一切，从而保证了它作为经典被接受。此外，艾鲁特神父在法国受教育，并用法语写作他的研究，作为法国大学的学位论文，这并非偶然。与阿拉伯文著作不同，它很容易被译成英文、俄文和美国版本。使这本书成为经典的最后一组机制，是战后美国政治的需要，特别是发展项目与大学中东课程的综合体。1945年的英文版通过人类关系区域档案在美国发行；显然，最初的美国译本是由美国“第四点计划”制作的，大概是用作美国发展专家了解埃及乡村的入门读物。
1963年灯塔出版社版终于出版时，《经济学人》自信地评论道：“关于纳赛尔总统在埃及乡村国内任务的艰巨程度，没有比这更好的书了。”

en: Despite its status as a classic, the book required updating for the American edition, and also some minor yet significant rewriting by the author. Several references to the political violence commonly used by Egyptian peasants against the authorities were deleted or amended in the U.S. edition, replacing them with an image of “passive and obedient” villagers. For example, the original text describes the reaction of a group of peasants to an attempt to take possession of their ʿizba (the workers’ housing complex on a large commercial estate, discussed in chapter 2, which often evolved into a self-contained village while the houses, fields, agricultural equipment, and even domestic animals remained the estate owner’s property) by a financial institution that had foreclosed on its owner:
zh: 尽管具有经典地位，这本书仍需要为美国版作更新，作者还作了一些细小却重要的改写。美国版删除或修改了若干处提及埃及农民惯常对当局使用政治暴力的文字，代之以“被动而顺从”的村民形象。例如，原文描述一群农民对一家金融机构试图占有其伊兹巴（ʿizba，即大型商业庄园上的工人住房群，已在第二章讨论过；它常常演变成一个自成一体的村庄，而房屋、田地、农业设备甚至家畜仍是庄园主的财产）的反应——该机构已对庄园主取消了抵押赎回权：

en: When the bank’s bailiff arrived to carry out the seizure, the villagers resisted him, and the police had to interfere. The assistant chief constable of the markaz [district] arrived on the scene at the head of an armed force, but was attacked by the people. Seeing that the situation promised to grow more serious, he felt himself obliged to order shots to be fired in the air to frighten the fellaheen. The effect was to exasperate them. They proceeded to cut the telephone wires and to burn the bailiff’s car. A new body of police soon came to the rescue, but proved as useless as the first. Finally the Mudeer [provincial governor] appeared on the scene at the head of yet a third force and order was re-established only when further shots had been fired into the air. Seven of the policemen were wounded by stones thrown at them by the villagers. Several villagers were arrested, and a judicial enquiry was opened. This incident, which took place in 1936, is by no means abnormal. (41–42)
zh: 银行法警抵达执行扣押时，村民抵抗他，警察不得不介入。区（markaz）助理警察局长率领一支武装力量到达现场，却遭到民众攻击。他见局势势必更加严重，觉得不得不下令向空中鸣枪以吓唬费拉欣。效果却是激怒了他们。他们接着割断电话线，烧毁法警的汽车。一批新的警察很快赶来救援，但证明和第一批一样无用。最后，省督（Mudeer）又率领第三支力量出现在现场；直到再次向空中鸣枪之后，秩序才得以恢复。七名警察被村民投掷的石块打伤。数名村民被捕，并开始了司法调查。这一事件发生在1936年，绝非异常。（41—42）

en: In the American edition this paragraph has been removed and replaced by a single sentence:“Occasionally it was necessary to put the ordinarily passive and obedient peasants down with police force.”

With such amendments some of the few references in Ayrout to particular historical and political episodes were eliminated, and the book’s portrayal of a hapless peasantry inhabiting a changeless countryside was ready for the American reader.
zh: 在美国版中，这一段被删去，代之以一句话：“偶尔有必要用警察武力镇压通常被动而顺从的农民。”
借助此类修改，艾鲁特书中少数提及具体历史和政治事件的地方被删除了，而该书对一个栖居在不变乡村中的无助农民阶层的描绘，也就为美国读者准备好了。

en: We can now return to Critchfield. We have seen how he invokes Ayrout to support the image of an Egyptian village unchanged in six thousand years, and we have seen the sources of these images in Ayrout, especially the borrowings from Le Bon, and their acceptance in the United States as a relevant and realistic portrayal of rural Egypt in the second half of the twentieth century. Critchfield’s role is to take up these fading images in the last quarter of the century and reprint them in new colors.
zh: 现在我们可以回到克里奇菲尔德。我们已经看到他如何援引艾鲁特，来支撑埃及村庄六千年不变的意象；我们也已看到这些意象在艾鲁特那里的来源，特别是对勒邦的借用，以及它们如何在美国被接受为对20世纪下半叶埃及乡村的一种切题而现实的描绘。克里奇菲尔德的作用，是在这个世纪的最后四分之一接续这些正在褪色的意象，并以新的色彩重新印出。

en: It is not just that Critchfield has read Ayrout before he arrives in the village and sees the place through the earlier text. Matters are much worse— he is unable to put Ayrout down. For example, when Critchfield goes with Shahhat to the local market (suq), he cannot help turning again to The Egyptian Peasant. The market, Ayrout had explained,
zh: 并不只是克里奇菲尔德在抵达村庄之前读过艾鲁特，并通过早先的文本观看这个地方。情况要糟得多——他放不下艾鲁特。例如，当克里奇菲尔德与沙哈特一起去当地市场（suq）时，他忍不住再次翻开《埃及农民》。艾鲁特曾解释说，市场

en: lasts from dawn to midday. The sellers . . . make their way to it at daybreak in long files, choose a spot to lay out their wares, and squat down behind them to wait for customers . . . . All is a noisy, confused mêlée of men, cattle and goods. (104)
zh: 从黎明持续到正午。卖主们……在天亮时排成长队赶去，选一块地方铺开货物，然后蹲在货物后面等候顾客……一切都是男人、牲畜和货物构成的一片喧闹混乱的混杂。（104）

en: “The suk,” Critchfield tells us,
zh: 克里奇菲尔德告诉我们，“suk（集市）”

en: lasted from dawn to mid-morning, and if Shahhat wanted to sell something, he came at daybreak, chose a spot along the road to display his vegetables or tether his sheep, and squatted down to wait for customers. By eight o’clock the suk was a noisy, confused hubbub of men, women, children, cattle, and goods. (86)
zh: 从黎明持续到上午过了一半；如果沙哈特想卖东西，他会在天亮时赶来，在路边选一块地方摆出蔬菜，或拴好他的羊，然后蹲下来等候顾客。到八点钟，集市已经是男人、女人、孩子、牲畜和货物构成的一片喧闹混乱的嘈杂。（86）

en: Further on Ayrout continued:
zh: 再往后，艾鲁特接着写道：

en: Here again can be seen the love of the fellaheen for crowding together and moving only in congested groups. If they have to cross the Nile . . . the fellaheen throng so densely into the ferry-boat . . . that accidents are frequent. When they set out on foot or on donkey-back, laden with astonishing bundles, it looks like an evacuation. . . . When they have to travel by train, they arrive several hours beforehand, cluster on a corner of the platform, and scramble all together into one carriage, even if there is plenty of room elsewhere. (106)
zh: 这里再次可以看到费拉欣对拥挤在一起、只在密集群体中行动的热爱。如果他们必须渡过尼罗河……费拉欣们会如此密集地挤进渡船……以致事故频发。当他们满载着惊人的包裹步行或骑驴出发时，看起来就像一场疏散……当他们必须乘火车时，会提前几个小时到达，聚在站台的一个角落，然后一起挤进同一节车厢，即使别处还有充足的空间。（106）

en: And Critchfield:
zh: 而克里奇菲尔德写道：

en: Though there was plenty of space along the road, they all crowded together in one small area for the fellaheen loved congested groups. When they crossed the Nile everyone would throng into the same small ferry so that it was a wonder accidents were rare. When they took the train, they would arrive two or three hours early, cluster on one end of the platform and then scramble all together into a single carriage, even if there was plenty of room in the next one. The road through the suk, with so many people hurrying by on donkey or on foot—most of them laden with enormous bundles . . . —resembled an evacuation. (86–87)
zh: 尽管沿路有充足的空间，他们却全都挤在一个小区块里，因为费拉欣热爱密集的群体。渡尼罗河时，每个人都挤进同一条小船，以至于事故竟然很少，实在令人惊奇。乘火车时，他们会提前两三个小时到达，聚在站台的一端，然后一起挤进单独一节车厢，即使下一节车厢还有充足的空间。穿过集市的那条路上，那么多人骑着驴或步行匆匆而过——大多数人满载着巨大的包裹……——看上去像一场疏散。（86—87）

en: But not as much as it resembled Ayrout’s book.
zh: 但远不如它像艾鲁特的书。

en: How do the characters in Critchfield’s drama cope with the strangely constructed world in which they find themselves? There is no problem, for they are constructed the same way. They are as preserved and repeated as the countryside they inhabit. In the chapter of his book “The Peasant’s Body,” Ayrout describes under the heading “Race and Type” the racial features of the Egyptian—drawing, incidentally, on the scientific racism of writers like Gustave Le Bon. Ayrout notes that the peasant of Upper Egypt, being a mixture of Egyptian and “negro,” is
zh: 克里奇菲尔德戏剧中的人物，如何应对他们发现自己身处其中的这个构造奇特的世界？没有问题，因为他们也是以同样的方式构造出来的。他们和他们所栖居的乡村一样，是保存下来并重复出来的。在其书“农民的身体”一章中，艾鲁特在“种族与类型”这一标题下描述了埃及人的种族特征——顺便说一句，他借用了古斯塔夫·勒邦之流作家的科学种族主义。艾鲁特指出，上埃及农民是埃及人与“黑种人”的混合，因此

en: heavily built [with] rather prominent cheekbones, a thick nose . . . and a heavy jaw. His features on the whole are rugged . . . neither very sensitive nor very expressive. [The Arab nomads] differ markedly from the fellaheen by their finer features . . . their more excitable temperament [and] their cruelty in vengeance. (79–80)
zh: 体格粗壮，［有］相当突出的颧骨、厚鼻子……和沉重的下颌。他的五官总体上粗犷……既不很敏感，也不很有表现力。［阿拉伯游牧者］与费拉欣明显不同：他们的五官更精细……性情更易激动，［以及］复仇时的残酷。（79—80）

en: Critchfield tells us that, “except for his curly black hair, with its hint of African negro blood,” Shahhat “looked more Arabian than Egyptian.” Most of the other young men in the village were
zh: 克里奇菲尔德告诉我们，“除了带有一丝非洲黑人血统痕迹的黑色卷发”，沙哈特“看起来更像阿拉伯人，而不像埃及人”。村里大多数其他年轻人则

en: more heavily built, and had strong cheekbones, thick noses, and heavy jaws. Among their rugged faces, Shahhat’s stood out as singularly sensitive and expressive. His finer, more Semitic features and more excitable temperament, his sense of vengeance that was not without its cruel side . . . (5)
zh: 体格更加粗壮，颧骨结实、鼻子粗厚、下颌沉重。在他们粗犷的面孔中间，沙哈特的脸显得格外敏感而富有表现力。他那更精细、更像闪米特人的五官和更易激动的性情，他那并非没有残酷一面的复仇意识……（5）

en: made Shahhat resemble the nomads of the desert—or at least the nomads of Ayrout’s racial classification.
zh: 使沙哈特像沙漠中的游牧者——至少像艾鲁特种族分类中的游牧者。

en: This racial vocabulary, once borrowed from Ayrout, recurs throughout Critchfield’s story. The “vengeful Bedouin streak in Shahhat’s blood” is continually invoked to explain his habitual violence (63). His friends and associates are contrastingly “negro.” In the “dark brown skin, curly hair, thick lips, and strong cheekbones” of his friend Snake, “there was something plainly African” (59); Faruk, Shahhat’s sharecropper, has “wet, open lips” (15), later described as “full, wet lips” (51); and Abdullahi, owner of the local bar, has a head and chest covered in “frizzy hair like a negro’s” (35). The racist effect is enhanced by most of the other descriptions of people’s facial features. Hagg Ali, for example, has “cunning, calculating eyes, a hawk nose, wrinkled face, and an ingratiating, obsequious manner” (20). When he gets annoyed this “cunning face” is “twisted into an angry, purple fury . . . the veins swelling on his forehead” (55). (Veins and muscles are continually swelling: when Shahhat gets angry his face and neck turn “crimson with all the muscles strained” [12], we meet another whose “neck muscles stood out like ropes” [74], and so on.) The face of Abdullahi, the bar owner, is “hideously pock-marked,” and those of his customers always have “a demoniac look” (35). Bahiya’s eyes are “dull and squinty,” whereas Suʿad has “sly, viperish eyes” (41–42). Sheikh al-Hufni is “a bent, emaciated, toothless old man” (44), as opposed to Yusef, who is “bent, toothless, and garrulous” (50). El Got is “a slight, weaselly, pale little man” (60); Mitri is “frail and wrinkled” like “an old gnome” with “rheumy blue eyes” (101); the father of Faruk, the sharecropper, is a “shrunken little man”; Hasan, a “drunken scoundrel,” has “such a short, thick neck he looked hunch-backed”; Ali, Hasan’s son, is a “dull, slack-jawed youth” (147–48); and so on.
zh: 这套从艾鲁特那里借来的种族词汇，在克里奇菲尔德的故事中反复出现。“沙哈特血液中那复仇的贝都因气质”不断被用来解释他惯常的暴力（63）。他的朋友和同伴则相反，是“黑人”。他的朋友斯内克“深棕色的皮肤、卷发、厚嘴唇和结实的颧骨”中，“明显有某种非洲的东西”（59）；沙哈特的佃农法鲁克有“湿润、张开的嘴唇”（15），后文又形容为“丰厚、湿润的嘴唇”（51）；当地酒吧老板阿卜杜拉希的头部和胸部则布满“像黑人一样的鬈发”（35）。大多数关于人物面部特征的其他描写强化了这种种族主义效果。例如哈吉·阿里有一双“狡黠、精于算计的眼睛，鹰钩鼻，布满皱纹的脸，以及一种讨好谄媚的举止”（20）。当他恼怒时，这张“狡黠的脸”便“扭曲成愤怒的紫色狂怒……额头上的青筋暴起”（55）。（青筋和肌肉不断暴起：沙哈特发怒时，他的脸和脖子“涨得通红，所有肌肉都绷紧了”［12］；我们又遇到一个人，“脖子上的肌肉像绳子一样凸起”［74］，等等。）酒吧老板阿卜杜拉希的脸“布满难看的麻点”，他的顾客们的脸则总是带着“一种恶魔般的神情”（35）。巴希娅的眼睛“呆滞而斜视”，而苏阿德有“阴险、毒蛇般的眼睛”（41—42）。谢赫·胡夫尼是“一个驼背、消瘦、没有牙齿的老人”（44），与之相对的是优素福，“驼背、没牙、爱唠叨”（50）。埃尔·戈特是“一个瘦小、黄鼠狼般、面色苍白的小个子”（60）；米特里“虚弱而布满皱纹”，像“一个老侏儒”，有一双“含泪的蓝眼睛”（101）；佃农法鲁克的父亲是一个“缩小了的小个子”；哈桑是个“酒鬼无赖”，脖子“又短又粗，使他看起来像驼背”；哈桑的儿子阿里是“一个迟钝、下巴松弛的青年”（147—148）；等等。

en: To complete the racist effect, these characters are all made to speak, as it were, like foreigners. None of them knows how to say “a lot,” for example, so they are always saying things like “there is much grain left” (155), “he must love money much” (120), and “in the past there was much wheat. . . . Now we cultivate sugar cane and oh, so many crops and get much money . . . [and] eat and drink much” (95).When a sharecropper gets dismissed he says, “All right. Finish. I wanted that” (150), and when Zacharias criticizes the government a woman announces “The speaking of Zacharias is good” (121). Someone leaving home says “Tell your mother goodbye. We go to Cairo” (205), and when he returns they say “Best arrival to you” (212), unless the arrival is unexpected, when they say “What a strange coming” (169).
zh: 为完成这种种族主义效果，这些人物的说话方式都被弄得——可以说——像外国人。例如，他们谁都不知道怎样说“a lot”（很多），于是总说“还剩很多粮食”（155）、“他一定爱钱很多”（120）以及“过去有很多小麦……现在我们种甘蔗，噢，那么多庄稼，得到很多钱……［还］吃很多、喝很多”（95）。一个佃农被解雇时说：“好吧。完了。那是我想要的”（150）；当扎卡里亚斯批评政府时，一个女人宣布：“扎卡里亚斯的说话是好的”（121）。有人离家时说：“告诉你母亲再见。我们去开罗”（205）；回来时他们说：“祝你最好的到达”（212），除非这次归来出人意料，那时他们便说：“多么奇怪的到来”（169）。

en: Within this racial framework, Shahhat’s whole character seems to have been determined in advance by Ayrout. “Rural, gregarious, stay-at-home; such is the Egyptian people in its dominant characteristics” (30), wrote Ayrout, noting later “their love of the soil, their sense of rhythm, and their taste for songs, stories and colours.”The peasant’s intellect, he said,“is controlled by his senses, and remains close to things felt and done. . . . Life to him is a succession but of todays” (133–34). Sure enough, Shahhat turns out to be “rural, gregarious, stay-at-home. . . . With his love for the soil, his feel for physical labor and nature’s rhythms, his taste for songs, stories and gossip, his mind was governed by the senses and stayed close to things done and felt; life to him was a succession of todays” (38). Not to mention a succession of plagiarisms.
zh: 在这一种族框架内，沙哈特的整个人物性格似乎已由艾鲁特预先确定。“乡土、群居、恋家；这就是埃及人的主导特征”（30），艾鲁特写道，随后又提到“他们对土地的热爱、他们的节奏感，以及他们对歌曲、故事和色彩的喜好”。他说，农民的智力“受感官支配，始终贴近被感受和被做了的事情……对他来说，生活不过是一个又一个今天接续而成”（133—134）。果然，沙哈特表现为“乡土、群居、恋家……他热爱土地，对体力劳动和自然的节奏有感受力，喜好歌曲、故事和闲谈，他的心智受感官支配，贴近做过和感受过的事情；对他来说，生活是一个又一个今天的接续”（38）。更不用说一连串的抄袭了。

en: Explaining the views on sexuality among his village hosts, Critchfield also borrows from Ayrout. “The temperament of the fellaheen,” Ayrout tells us,
zh: 在解释他村中主人对性的看法时，克里奇菲尔德也借用了艾鲁特。艾鲁特告诉我们：“费拉欣的性情

en: is very ardent and sensual . . . [but] the heat of passion is short-lived. At thirty a fellah woman is no longer attractive, but the children she has borne her husband bind him to her. . . . The men . . . are kept faithful less by virtue than by village law. (119)
zh: 非常热烈而耽于肉欲……［但］激情的热度是短暂的。费拉赫女人到三十岁便不再有吸引力，但她为丈夫生下的孩子把他与她绑在一起……男人们……与其说是靠美德，不如说是靠乡村的法律保持忠诚。（119）

en: According to Critchfield,
zh: 据克里奇菲尔德说，

en: Ommohamed [Shahhat’s mother] knew that young men like Shahhat were ardent, sensual, and romantic, but that the heat of such passion
zh: 乌姆穆罕默德［沙哈特的母亲］知道，像沙哈特这样的年轻男子热烈、耽于肉欲而浪漫，但这种激情的热度

en: cooled all too soon; after thirty or so it was the children . . . that bound a husband and wife together. In her eyes men were kept in place less by their own virtue than by Islamic law and village social pressure. (29–30)
zh: 冷却得太快；大约三十岁以后，把他们夫妻绑在一起的便是孩子……。在她眼里，男人守规矩，与其说是靠自己的美德，不如说是靠伊斯兰法和村庄的社会压力。（29—30）

en: Perhaps even Ommohamed had been reading Ayrout.
zh: 也许连乌姆穆罕默德也读过艾鲁特。

en: Taking his cue from Ayrout, Critchfield turns the sexuality and violence of villagers into a major theme of the book. His Author’s Note at the beginning suggests that in Upper Egyptian villages “the occurrence of adultery, fornication, and sodomy, despite severe Moslem penalties, seems an assertion of pagan sensuality absent elsewhere in Egypt” (xv).The opening pages set the scene by invoking ancient Egypt as the source of this obscene and violent paganism. Shahhat’s mother is described, twenty years earlier, stealthily entering the ruins of a temple at night and observing the local Pharaonic art. There are wall paintings portraying “a procession led by the god of the penis,” and reliefs depicting the pharaoh’s military victories that show “mass decapitations and castrations, with heaps of genitals carved in stone.” The very sight of these genital heaps, we are told, causes local villagers to become “filled with lust” (9). Soon after we are informed of the young Shahhat’s “growing sexual hunger” and told how “the size of his penis” became the object of village comment. Pride in their masculinity, it seems, creates in local men “a drive to reduce competing males to lesser status through domination, sadism, and even sodomy; dominance was everything.” It comes as no surprise that the villagers, described in this way as animals, commonly practice sodomy not just with other males but with animals, too. Shahhat himself, Critchfield informs us, used to do it with a female donkey (17).
zh: 克里奇菲尔德追随艾鲁特的思路，把村民的性与暴力变成书中的一个重要主题。书前的“作者说明”提出，在上埃及村庄里，“通奸、私通和鸡奸的发生，尽管有严厉的穆斯林惩罚，似乎是一种异教肉欲的宣示，在埃及其他地方并不存在”（xv）。开篇几页援引古埃及作为这种淫秽而暴力的异教信仰的来源。书中描述，二十年前，沙哈特的母亲在夜里悄悄进入一座神庙废墟，观看当地的法老艺术。那里有壁画描绘“由阴茎之神引领的游行队伍”，还有表现法老军事胜利的浮雕，上面显示“成批的斩首与阉割，以及刻在石头上的一堆堆生殖器”。据说，一见到这些生殖器堆，当地村民便“充满淫欲”（9）。不久之后，我们得知年轻的沙哈特“日益增长的性饥渴”，并得知“他阴茎的尺寸”如何成为村里人议论的对象。看来，对男子气概的骄傲在当地男人心中造成一种“通过支配、施虐甚至鸡奸，把竞争的男性贬低到较低地位的冲动；支配就是一切”。难怪这些被如此描述为动物般的村民，不仅常与其他男性鸡奸，也与动物鸡奸。克里奇菲尔德告诉我们，沙哈特本人就曾与一头母驴做这种事（17）。

en: The rest of the book follows in much the same tone, telling us, page after page, of fights and stabbings and robberies and murders, of men who rape, men who bite off people’s noses, and men who kill people and cut them into little pieces. Most of these events occurred before Critchfield came to the village, or while he was away in Cairo, and are related to him second- or third-hand by Shahhat, through an interpreter. Their secondhand quality is obvious. One story, for example, involves Shahhat’s sharecropper, Faruk, a “drunkard and voluptuary” according to the caption under his photograph, who is involved in “every sort of debauchery, drinking heavily, smoking hashish, chasing women, and spending long hours gambling” (16). One night, we are told, he met in the fields with a woman from a nearby village who used to sell herself occasionally for money. The couple were discovered, however, by two other villagers—”coarse, filthy, dishonest and drunken men”—who hit the woman, beat Faruk and tied him up, stripped the woman naked, and took turns raping her, pausing when they were finished to untie Faruk and beat him again, “pounding and kicking him until he lost his senses.”Almost every line of the story is clichéd, from “Faruk could not tear his eyes away as he listened to the woman’s moans,” to the description of the woman’s breasts as, inevitably, “full” and “firm.” We are also told by the author that she enjoyed being raped (78–79). The book’s tone is persistently misogynist; another rape victim is shown in a photograph, smiling at the camera, with a caption that describes her as a “willful, flirtatious fourteen-year-old” (103).
zh: 书的其余部分以大致相同的调子继续，一页又一页地告诉我们斗殴、刀刺、抢劫和谋杀，告诉我们有男人强奸、有男人咬掉别人的鼻子、有男人把人杀死并剁成小块。这些事件大多发生在克里奇菲尔德来到村庄之前，或发生在他去开罗的时候，由沙哈特通过一名译员二传或三传告诉他。它们的二手性质显而易见。例如，有一个故事涉及沙哈特的佃农法鲁克，他照片下的说明称其为“酒鬼和淫棍”，卷入“各种各样的放荡：酗酒、抽大麻、追逐女人，还长时间赌博”（16）。据说有一天夜里，他在田野里遇到邻近村庄的一个女人，她过去偶尔卖身赚钱。然而，这对男女被另外两个村民发现了——“粗俗、肮脏、不诚实、酗酒的男人”——他们殴打那个女人，把法鲁克痛打一顿并捆起来，把女人剥光，轮流强奸她，完事后停下来解开法鲁克，再打他一顿，“拳打脚踢，直到他失去知觉”。这个故事几乎每一行都是陈词滥调，从“法鲁克听着女人的呻吟，无法移开目光”，到把女人的乳房照例描写成“丰满”而“结实”。作者还告诉我们，她喜欢被强奸（78—79）。全书的调子始终带有厌女色彩；另一名强奸受害者出现在一张照片里，对着镜头微笑，照片说明称她是一个“任性、调情的十四岁女孩”（103）。

en: Critchfield retells this tale not as an example of how a vexatious village youth offers colorful stories to a visiting American, but as a detail for his picture of what villagers, as Professor Foster’s foreword puts it, are really like (indeed, Foster particularly praises Critchfield for bringing into view the “darker side” of peasant behavior—which, he assures us, given the peasants’ poverty and lack of opportunity,“is highly adaptive” [x]). Critchfield’s factual presentation of such episodes is especially surprising given that he admits elsewhere in the book that local stories could become “exaggerated and dramatized” as they “spread through the village” (139), and that Shahhat in particular “had ceased to be able to distinguish” between tales he had heard from others and those he had invented himself. “The most fantastic unreality easily paled and mingled with the real.” An “educated outsider,” Critchfield adds, “might be expected to grow bored and skeptical” (100).
zh: 克里奇菲尔德重述这个故事，并不是把它当作一个例子，说明一个讨人厌的乡村青年如何向来访的美国人讲述色彩斑斓的故事，而是把它当作一个细节，用来描绘福斯特教授序言所说的村民的真实面貌（事实上，福斯特特别赞扬克里奇菲尔德呈现了农民行为中的“阴暗面”——他向我们保证，考虑到农民的贫困和缺乏机会，这种阴暗面“具有很强的适应性”［x］）。克里奇菲尔德对这类事件所作的事实化呈现尤其令人惊讶，因为他在书中别处承认，当地的故事在“传遍村庄”时会变得“夸张和戏剧化”（139），而沙哈特尤其“已经无法区分”他从别人那里听来的故事和他自己编造的故事。“最离奇的虚幻轻易地褪色，与真实混在一起。”克里奇菲尔德补充说，“受过教育的局外人或许会感到厌倦并产生怀疑”（100）。

en: He or she might indeed—especially as Critchfield seems to share Shahhat’s problem of being unable to distinguish the unreal from the real, and with the help of Ayrout has put some additional tales of violence into the mouths of his informants. Describing the military conscription of the peasant, Ayrout had explained that
zh: 他或她确实可能会——尤其因为克里奇菲尔德似乎和沙哈特一样，有无法区分虚幻与真实的问题，并且在艾鲁特的帮助下，把另外一些暴力故事塞进了他报道提供者的嘴里。在描述农民被征兵时，艾鲁特曾解释说，

en: to ensure his rejection he may put out one of his eyes, or cut off a couple of fingers. . . . If he can, he will hide or escape. . . . When there is no way out, and he cannot avoid leaving home to join the army, the family receives condolences and abandons itself to mourning as if for a bereavement. To leave the village is like going abroad. Partir, c’est mourir. (107)
zh: 为确保自己不被录取，他可能会挖掉一只眼睛，或切掉两根手指……如果办得到，他会躲起来或逃走……当无路可走、无法避免离家参军时，家里人会接受吊唁，陷入哀悼，仿佛遭遇了丧亲之痛。离开村庄就像出国。Partir, c'est mourir（离去即死亡）。（107）

en: Critchfield relates that
zh: 克里奇菲尔德讲述道，

en: Shahhat had heard how in past times young men in the village had been known to cut off their fingers or put out an eye to be rejected, or try to hide in the desert to escape. If there was no way out and they
zh: 沙哈特听说过，过去村里有年轻人为了不被录取而切掉手指或挖掉眼睛，或者试图藏到沙漠里逃跑。如果无路可走，他们

en: could not avoid going into the army, their families received condolences and abandoned themselves to formal mourning as if their sons were already dead. In the old days, to leave the village was to die. (162)
zh: 无法避免参军，家里人会接受吊唁，正式陷入哀悼，仿佛儿子已经死了。在过去，离开村庄就等于死亡。（162）

en: Describing the working of vendettas in rural Egypt, Ayrout had said that sometimes
zh: 在描述埃及乡村血仇的运作时，艾鲁特曾说，有时

en: the feud is kept up in every family from generation to generation. . . . The antagonism, though usually latent, will show itself suddenly over some trivial matter, such as the shifting of a boundary mark, a theft of manure, or a gamoossa trespassing. Then human life counts for nothing. (109)
zh: 血仇在每一代、每一个家庭中延续……敌意虽然通常潜伏，却会因一些琐事突然显现，比如移动界标、偷粪肥，或一头水牛误入他人田地。那时人命就一文不值了。（109）

en: Critchfield tells us that even in Buʿairat
zh: 克里奇菲尔德告诉我们，即使在布艾拉特，

en: a feud, once started over a diesel pump or some other trivial affair, could go on a long time. Antagonism might show itself over something so trifling as a trespassing sheep, missing fodder, or the shifting of a boundary marker, and before long it could seem as if human life counted for nothing. (89)
zh: 一场血仇一旦因柴油泵或其他琐事而起，就可能持续很久。敌意可能因一只误入的羊、丢失的饲料或移动界标之类微不足道的事情而显现，要不了多久，人命似乎就变得一文不值。（89）

en: Ayrout’s account had continued:
zh: 艾鲁特的叙述还继续写道：

en: Thus life is lived in constant insecurity. To feel this one must spend a night in a village. As soon as night falls . . . the dogs begin to bark . . .
zh: 因此，生活是在持续的不安全感中度过的。要感受这一点，必须在村庄里过一夜。夜幕一降临……狗就开始吠叫……

en: He goes on to describe an incident in the village of Qalandol in 1936 (another of the historical episodes eliminated from the U.S. edition of the book), where to avenge an earlier killing in a struggle over the selection of the village headman, a man was stabbed in the marketplace. The victim’s friends then
zh: 他接着描述1936年卡兰多尔村的一起事件（这是另一个从美国版中删去的历史插曲）：为报复此前在村长人选之争中的一起杀人事件，一名男子在市场里被刺伤。受害者的朋友们随后

en: bore down on the spot with rifles and staves, crying “Allah, Allah!” . . . By midnight the two parties [were] determined to fight to the death. . . . The police had the greatest difficulty in restoring order. (109–10)
zh: 带着步枪和棍棒冲向现场，高喊“安拉，安拉！”……到午夜，两方［已］决心决一死战……警察费了极大的力气才恢复秩序。（109—110）

en: Critchfield’s passage continues with a description of the village adjacent to Buʿairat:
zh: 克里奇菲尔德的段落接着描述与布艾拉特相邻的村庄：

en: But in Qurna life was lived in constant insecurity. As night fell, the dogs would start to roam and bark. . . . Sometimes a fight could start for no good reason and before long men would come running to reinforce both sides, armed with rifles and staves and shouting “Allah, Allah!” In no time both parties would vow to fight to the death and the police faced great difficulty in restoring order. (89)
zh: 但在古尔纳，生活是在持续的不安全感中度过的。夜幕降临时，狗便开始四处游荡、吠叫……有时一场打斗会毫无来由地开始，要不了多久，男人们就会带着步枪和棍棒跑来增援双方，高喊“安拉，安拉！”转眼间双方便发誓决一死战，警察要恢复秩序极为困难。（89）

en: Note that in Ayrout’s story the violence arose out of a serious political dispute, whereas the only point of originality in Critchfield’s version is that violence now occurs “for no good reason.”
zh: 请注意，在艾鲁特的故事里，暴力源于一场严肃的政治争端，而克里奇菲尔德版本中唯一具有原创性的地方，是暴力如今发生在“毫无正当理由”的情况下。

en: In this construction of what the Egyptian—and Third World—peasant is “really like,” there is more than just a persistent plagiarism and the addition of invented incidents. There is also something missing. The account is written entirely in the third person, rendering the author, who was partly present in the village, completely absent from the scene. Critchfield only presents himself at the end, in an afterword, in which there is a photograph of him standing in the village and a careful explanation of his method. He always begins the study of a “traditional village” by laboring in the fields, working alongside the person he refers to, using the possessive, as “my peasant subject.” He then works with interpreters, using two of them a day (“interpreters tend to tire after five or six hours of steady translation”), to compile a voluminous ledger of his subject’s recollections of past adventures and dialogues. “These became seven hundred pages of single-spaced typewritten notes,” we are told. “Shahhat and I,” the author adds, “were together, virtually every waking hour, for almost a year” (227–31). Moreover, we have been assured in the preface that the names of the characters in the story, as well as the photographs that illustrate it, are all “real” (xiv).The result is “as true a portrait” as he can write, Critchfield concludes, ending the book with a circular, almost desperate, assertion about Shahhat’s story: “A real person, his identity and existence are its verification” (233).The claims, the details of how the account was constructed, and the confidential and possessive tone in which they are imparted to us—all placed outside the telling of the story itself—are intended to establish the author’s authority.
zh: 在这样建构埃及——以及第三世界——农民“实际上是什么样子”的过程中，不仅有持续不断的抄袭和添加虚构事件，还有某种缺失。全书记述完全用第三人称写成，使那位部分时间身在村庄的作者完全不出现在场景中。克里奇菲尔德只在最后的后记中露面；后记中有一张他站在村里的照片，还有对其方法的详细说明。他研究“传统村庄”时，总是先在田里干活，与他用所有格称作“我的农民研究对象”的人并肩劳作。然后他与译员合作，每天用两名（“译员在连续翻译五六个小时后容易疲倦”），编成一本厚厚的账簿，记录研究对象对往日冒险和对话的回忆。“这些变成了七百页单倍行距的打字笔记，”我们得知。作者补充说：“沙哈特和我，几乎每一个醒着的时辰都在一起，持续了将近一年”（227—231）。此外，序言向我们保证，故事中人物的姓名以及书中所附照片，都是“真实的”（xiv）。克里奇菲尔德总结道，其成果是他所能写出的“尽可能真实的画像”；全书以一句循环式的、几乎绝望的断言收尾，谈沙哈特的故事：“一个真实的人，他的身份和存在就是它的验证”（233）。这些声明、关于记述如何建构的细节，以及向我们传达这些内容时那种私密而带占有欲的口吻——全都被置于故事叙述之外——意在确立作者的权威。

en: While in the village, Critchfield adds in the afterword, he and his interpreter “tried, as much as we were able, to remain observers and not participants, and I think, in the main, we succeeded.” But this required the “restraining influence” of the interpreter, for on several occasions, Critchfield informs us in the same paragraph, he and his peasant subject “had violent, usually drunken fights, Arab-fashion, coming to blows, once throwing chairs at each other, and sometimes actually knocking each other down.” Although these bouts of “Arab” violence left the villagers “always upset,” the American “rather enjoyed them,” as did his subject. “With the possible exception of one or two other peasant subjects, I doubt if I have ever gotten to know anyone, including members of my own family, as intimately as I grew to know Shahhat.” This intimacy, secretly confided to us, is intended to increase rather than undermine the author’s authority, for apparently it has nothing to do with what Critchfield calls “the story”: “when it came to events that represented progress in the story, [the interpreter] and I kept carefully aside” (231–32). Thus the device of the confessional afterword assures us of the author’s intimate understanding, while the removal of all traces of the author’s presence from the story itself creates an effect of objectivity.
zh: 克里奇菲尔德在后记中补充说，在村里期间，他和译员“尽力保持观察者而非参与者的身份，我认为我们大体上做到了”。但这需要译员的“约束作用”，因为克里奇菲尔德在同一段中告诉我们，有几次他和他的农民研究对象“像阿拉伯人那样发生了激烈的、通常是醉后的打斗，动了拳头，有一次还互扔椅子，有时真的把对方打倒在地”。尽管这些“阿拉伯式”的暴力冲突让村民“总是心烦意乱”，这位美国人却“相当喜欢”它们，他的研究对象也是如此。“除了可能有一两个其他农民研究对象，我怀疑我是否曾像了解沙哈特那样，亲密地了解任何人，包括我自己的家人。”这种私密关系被偷偷告诉我们，意在增强而非削弱作者的权威，因为显然它与克里奇菲尔德所说的“故事”无关：“当涉及推动故事进展的事件时，［译员］和我都小心翼翼地置身一旁”（231—232）。于是，忏悔式后记的手法使我们确信作者有深入的理解，而把作者在场的一切痕迹从故事本身中清除，则制造出一种客观性的效果。

en: In my own copy of Shahhat, however, some of the book’s pages are bound out of place, with the result that a part of the afterword comes in the middle of the “story.” In the heat of a violent quarrel Shahhat is having with his mother and uncle, which causes him to leave the village for Cairo, Critchfield himself accidentally appears, speaking to us in the first person: “Advised of the quarrel by Shahhat in Cairo, I returned once more to the village. Hence I was physically present during the more dramatic episodes of the closing section.” In one of these episodes, he mentions, “I had to throw a violently hysterical scene” (230–32). After one more misplaced page we return to these very episodes, which are now haunted by this invisible, inadvertently announced presence. The separation of the author from his story is subverted, and the effect of objectivity slips away.
zh: 然而，在我自己那本《沙哈特》中，有些书页装订错了位置，结果后记的一部分出现在“故事”中间。沙哈特与母亲和叔叔发生激烈争吵，随后离村前往开罗；就在这场争吵最激烈的时候，克里奇菲尔德本人意外出现，用第一人称对我们说话：“在开罗从沙哈特那里得知这场争吵后，我又一次回到村里。因此，在结尾部分更富戏剧性的一些事件发生时，我本人就在现场。”在其中一件事中，他提到，“我不得不大闹一场歇斯底里的戏”（230—232）。又经过一页错装的书页，我们回到的正是这些事件，而此时它们已被这个看不见的、无意中宣告的在场所缠绕。作者与其故事之间的分隔被颠覆了，客观性的效果悄然溜走。

en: Yet even if your own copy of the book is correctly bound, you will sense another subversive presence haunting its pages. The storytelling elides the presence not only of the American author, but of the Westerner in general. The Western tourists and archaeologists who frequent the village and its surroundings are mentioned, but only obliquely and at a distance. Like the author, they are never allowed a presence of their own. The only straightforward account of them is the humorous description of a fleeting visit by a busload of tourists to the local Pharaonic temple. The sudden intrusion is shown strictly from the villagers’ point of view: the village square is shaken into life, chairs are put out in front of the café, Coca Cola and fake antiques are brought out to peddle, children demand baksheesh, and guides shout their instructions to the harried visitors. Then suddenly the bus is gone again, and the village regains its peace and quiet (107). Nevertheless, despite this deliberate distancing of the American and European presence, several other signs slip in to indicate a more pervasive relationship.
zh: 然而，即使你那本书装订正确，你也会感到书页间萦绕着另一种颠覆性的在场。故事的叙述删去了美国作者的在场，也删去了西方人总体的在场。经常出入村庄及其周边的西方游客和考古学家被提到了，但只是间接地、远远地提到。像作者一样，他们从未被允许拥有自己的在场。关于他们唯一直白的记述，是对一车游客匆匆造访当地法老神庙的幽默描写。这一突然闯入完全是从村民的视角呈现的：村中广场被惊动起来，咖啡馆门前摆出椅子，可口可乐和假古董被拿出来兜售，孩子们讨要小费，导游向疲惫不堪的游客大声发出指示。然后大巴突然又开走了，村庄恢复了安宁（107）。尽管如此，尽管有意拉开美国人和欧洲人存在的距离，书中还是溜进了其他一些迹象，表明一种更为普遍的关系。

en: First there is the Habu Hotel, built in the early 1960s, where Critchfield himself stayed. He describes it disingenuously as a “country inn” (227). As far as I know, however, it catered not to local travelers but largely to northern Europeans, attracted across the river from Luxor by the cheap rates for rooms and the even cheaper rates for local hashish. The village café, where Critchfield often spent his evenings, seems to have catered to a similar clientele; it was where villagers learned their English. Several of the key characters in the story earn their livelihoods and have even made fortunes from tourism or archaeology. Shahhat’s uncle, Ahmed, who we are told represents in the story the kind of Egyptian that “accepts modernization and its values” (xiv), works as a night watchman at the largest tourist hotel in Luxor (30). His father’s cousin, the notorious Hagg Ali,“had grown mysteriously rich in a short time,” allegedly from illicit dealing in archaeological treasures (19). He also organizes the supply of laborers for American archaeological digs all over Egypt, and is well known to organizations like the American Research Center in Egypt. Archaeology and tourism, in fact, appear to be a significant source of income for the village and certainly an integral part of its life. One or two more successful villagers have themselves become Egyptologists, including a man from the village who went on to study for a French doctorate at Montpellier and became a professor of Egyptology in Cairo.
zh: 首先是克里奇菲尔德本人下榻的哈布旅馆，建于1960年代初。他故作天真地把它描述成一家“乡村客栈”（227）。但据我所知，它并不招待本地旅客，而主要招待北欧人；这些人被低廉的房价和更便宜的大麻价格从卢克索吸引过河而来。克里奇菲尔德常在那里消磨夜晚的村中咖啡馆，似乎也招待类似的顾客；村民们正是在那里学会了英语。故事中若干关键人物靠旅游或考古谋生，甚至发了财。沙哈特的叔叔艾哈迈德——据说他在故事中代表“接受现代化及其价值观”的那类埃及人（xiv）——在卢克索最大的旅游旅馆当守夜人（30）。他父亲的表弟、臭名昭著的哈吉·阿里“在很短时间里神秘地发财”，据称是靠非法买卖考古珍宝（19）。他还为遍布埃及的美国考古发掘组织劳动力供应，并且在开罗美国研究中心之类的组织中很有名气。事实上，考古和旅游似乎是这个村庄的一项重要收入来源，也无疑是其生活不可分割的一部分。一两个较成功的村民自己成了埃及学家，其中包括村里的一位男子，他后来在蒙彼利埃攻读法国博士学位，并成为开罗的埃及学教授。

en: The book ignores the village’s dependence on archaeology and tourism, just as it ignores Shahhat’s dependence on the author. Critchfield arrived in Buʿairat just after the death of Shahhat’s father, when the boy’s family suddenly found itself seriously in debt. The opportune arrival of an American writer, willing to pay a village youth for his stories, can hardly have been irrelevant to the relationship that developed between them. Yet these forms of dependency upon Westerners and the Western economy are not discussed (“spending patterns remain traditional,” we are told [xviii]), and there is no attempt to analyze the larger causes of local poverty and debt essential to such dependence. The story is one of “cultural and psychological turbulence,” and the closest it comes to discussing economic dependence is a passing reference to the male prostitution that is often part of these contemporary forms of the colonial relationship. Shahhat’s friend Snake had often told Shahhat, who in turn had told Critchfield, “that if the foreign tourists who came to visit the tombs of Qurna were more interested in himself than the fake antiques he peddled, he took them out into the desert, where he would provide any service, as long as he was paid handsomely. It was not an uncommon way of earning money among the young men of Qurna.” But Shahhat himself, we are reassured immediately, “had little to do with tourists” (107).
zh: 这本书忽视了村庄对考古和旅游的依赖，正如它忽视了沙哈特对作者的依赖。克里奇菲尔德抵达布艾拉特时，沙哈特的父亲刚刚去世，这个男孩的家庭突然发现自己负债累累。一位美国作家恰在此时到来，愿意付钱让一个乡村青年讲述自己的故事，这很难说与他们之间发展出的关系无关。然而，这些依赖西方人和西方经济的形式并未得到讨论（我们被告知“消费模式仍很传统”［xviii］），也没有尝试分析当地贫困与债务的更大成因，而这些对于此种依赖至关重要。故事讲述的是“文化与心理动荡”，而它最接近讨论经济依赖的地方，只是顺带提到男性卖淫，这常常是当代殖民关系的这些形式的一部分。沙哈特的朋友斯内克常对沙哈特说，沙哈特又转告克里奇菲尔德，“如果来古尔纳参观陵墓的外国游客对他本人比对他兜售的假古董更感兴趣，他就把他们带到沙漠里，在那里提供任何服务，只要报酬优厚。这在古尔纳的年轻人中并非罕见的赚钱方式。”但我们立刻得到保证，沙哈特本人“与游客很少往来”（107）。

en: Since the 1970s tourism has become the largest industry in the Nile valley in terms of foreign earnings. Shahhat’s village might actually be somewhat “typical,” therefore, although not in any of the ways Critchfield suggests. In its inhabitants’ employment as peddlers, guides, café owners, hotel staff, part-time prostitutes, archaeological laborers, and native informants, the village perhaps typifies some of the novel ways in which the world of the West reorganized areas such as rural Egypt in the late twentieth century, and put the villager once more to work. Thus by eliding the presence of the tourist and archaeological industries, as well as his own presence as a writer, Critchfield helps conceal the multiple ways in which villagers continue to be organized as producers for nonvillage consumption.
zh: 1970年代以来，就外汇收入而言，旅游业已成为尼罗河谷最大的产业。因此，沙哈特的村庄实际上可能多少有些“典型”，尽管不是以克里奇菲尔德所暗示的任何方式。就村民充当小贩、导游、咖啡馆老板、旅馆员工、兼职妓女、考古劳工和土著报道人而言，这个村庄或许典型地体现了西方世界在20世纪末重组埃及乡村这类地区、并使村民再次投入工作的某些新方式。因此，通过删去旅游业和考古业的在场，以及他本人作为作家的在场，克里奇菲尔德帮助掩盖了村民继续被组织起来、为非村庄消费进行生产的多种方式。

en: Concealment, however, is the wrong word, for Shahhat itself forms a part of this system of production. Its role is to produce the peasant voice. Although we are assured in the afterword that Shahhat “knew no English” when Critchfield first met him, we have been told in the story itself that he had picked up some English “listening to foreigners in the café.” But, it is quickly added, “he never talked with them. If his friends asked why, he would say, ‘God gives me my work. I have land. Why should I speak with these foreigners . . . ? My work is to cultivate the land’ “ (228, 108). Until, of course, Critchfield arrived at the Habu Hotel and finally persuaded the peasant boy to speak. Thanks to Critchfield, as Foster puts it in his foreword, “Shahhat the man speaks for and to us” (xii). Just as Ayrout put into words for us the misery of peasants who were unable to feel their own suffering, Critchfield translates for us the words of a peasant who knows no English, enabling him finally to find a voice and communicate with us.
zh: 然而，“掩盖”这个词并不恰当，因为《沙哈特》本身构成了这一生产体系的一部分。它的作用是生产农民的声音。后记向我们保证，克里奇菲尔德最初遇见沙哈特时，他“不懂英语”；但故事本身又告诉我们，他“在咖啡馆听外国人说话”时学会了一些英语。不过紧接着又补充说，“他从不与他们交谈。如果朋友们问为什么，他会说：‘上帝给我工作。我有土地。我为什么要和这些外国人说话……？我的工作是种地’”（228，108）。当然，直到克里奇菲尔德来到哈布旅馆，终于说服这个农家男孩开口。正如福斯特在序言中所说，“多亏克里奇菲尔德，沙哈特这个人代表我们并向我们说话”（xii）。正如艾鲁特替我们说出那些无法感受自身苦难的农民的痛苦，克里奇菲尔德替我们翻译了一个不懂英语的农民的话，使他终于能够找到声音并与我们交流。

en: In this way, removing from the village both the presence of the American author and the playing of the world economy creates not just an effect of objectivity but also of a peasant subjectivity. Like many infinitely more respectable studies of the Third World peasant, Critchfield’s writing produces a peasant voice that appears self-formed. The voice is presented not as the product of an American writer, or even of the peasant’s encounter with the writer or with other local forms of Western hegemony, but as the speaking of an autonomous subject. Thanks to the invisible writer, the figure of the peasant is given a place in the monologue of the West, reaffirming with his presence our myth of partaking in a universal human dialogue. In this manner the peasant subject is produced for nonpeasant consumption, packaged by a university press and sold in the tourist hotels of Luxor and Cairo and the campus bookstores of American universities.
zh: 这样一来，从村庄中同时移除美国作者的在场和世界经济的运作，不仅制造出客观性的效果，也制造出农民主体性的效果。像许多远为体面的第三世界农民研究一样，克里奇菲尔德的写作生产出一种看起来自我形成的农民声音。这个声音不是作为美国作家的产品被呈现，甚至也不是作为农民与作家相遇、或与西方霸权其他当地形式相遇的产物，而是作为一个自主主体的言说。由于那位看不见的作家，农民的形象在西方独白中获得了一个位置，以他的在场重申了我们参与普遍人类对话的神话。农民主体就这样为非农民的消费而生产出来，由一家大学出版社包装，在卢克索和开罗的旅游旅馆以及美国大学的校园书店里出售。

en: Should Critchfield’s book be dismissed as merely an unfortunate and isolated case of plagiarism by an author who is more a popularizer than a scholar? After all, it might be said, he is clearly an enthusiastic writer whose sense of adventure and evident enjoyment of the company of some of those he writes about gave him a far greater exposure to villages around the world than any of his former colleagues among American foreign correspondents. I do not think so; not just because inserting the missing quotation marks around the passages plagiarized from Ayrout would do little to improve things, but because, in the years since its publication, the book itself and the realism it claims to present have never been dismissed. The problem posed by Shahhat is not primarily a question of plagiarism, but the question of why a book that reproduces yet again the racist stereotype of the Third World peasant, with all colonial history removed and all the effects of neocolonialism made invisible, can still be so easily and widely accepted.
zh: 是否应当把克里奇菲尔德的书仅仅当作一个不幸而孤立的抄袭案例，出自一位与其说是学者、不如说是普及者的人之手而不予理会？毕竟，人们可能会说，他显然是一位热情的作家，他的冒险意识以及他显然乐于与笔下某些人交往，使他比任何昔日的美国驻外记者同行都更多地接触了世界各地的村庄。我不这样认为；不仅因为给那些从艾鲁特那里抄袭的段落补上缺失的引号并不能改善多少，而且因为该书出版这些年来，书本身及其声称呈现的现实主义从未被摒弃。《沙哈特》所提出的问题主要不是抄袭问题，而是这样一个问题：为什么一本再次复制第三世界农民种族主义刻板印象、抹去一切殖民历史、使新殖民主义的一切后果不可见的书，仍然能够如此轻易地被广泛接受。
