en: Shahhat was described in the American Anthropologist as “an excellent dramatization of peasant life,” in the Journal of American Folklore as “enjoyable and readable,” and in the American Ethnologist as capturing, despite its “undisciplined subjectivity,” “the vividness and passionate intensity of Upper Egyptian life.”

George Foster’s foreword calls the book “one of the most absorbing accounts of peasant life I have ever read,” and stresses “the extent to which it illuminates and confirms the points anthropologists have made about peasant society” (xii). A note at the beginning of the book informs us that Richard Critchfield writes about the Third World for the Economist, the New York Times, the Los Angeles Times, the Christian Science Monitor, the Washington Post, Foreign Affairs, and the New Republic and is the author of numerous other books and articles about peasant life. These include a subsequent work, Villages (1981), in which he updates the story of Shahhat and gives what he admits are brief, “rambling” accounts of about a dozen other villages he has visited, including those from his days in Vietnam.“Somewhat unexpectedly,” we are told in the paperback edition, Villages “drew serious attention from agricultural scientists, students of development, and Washington policymakers.”
In 1988 Critchfield’s first book on peasants, The Golden Bowl Be Broken: Peasant Life in Four Cultures, was republished by a university press as a text “recommended for course use.”

Critchfield’s research in Egypt was financed with a grant from the Ford Foundation (and he subsequently received grants from the Rockefeller and other foundations and was employed as a consultant on Third World villages by the U.S. Agency for International Development. His “realism” in the portrayal of the peasant was supported, in other words, by a mass of reviewers, editors, publishers, development experts, policy makers, grant committee members, and university teachers.
zh: 《沙哈特》在《美国人类学家》中被称为“对农民生活的出色戏剧化”，在《美国民俗杂志》中被评为“令人愉快、可读性强”，在《美国民族学家》中则被说成尽管有“缺乏学科训练的主观性”，却捕捉到了“上埃及生活的生动与炽烈强度”。

乔治·福斯特的序言称这本书是“我读过的最引人入胜的农民生活记述之一”，并强调“它在多大程度上阐明并印证了人类学家关于农民社会的论点”（xii）。书前一则说明告诉我们，理查德·克里奇菲尔德为《经济学人》《纽约时报》《洛杉矶时报》《基督教科学箴言报》《华盛顿邮报》《外交事务》和《新共和》撰写关于第三世界的文章，还著有大量其他关于农民生活的书籍和文章。这些著作包括后来的《村庄》（1981）；他在书中更新了沙哈特的故事，并对他访问过的另外十几个村庄作了简短、他自己承认“东拉西扯”的记述，其中包括他在越南时期的见闻。平装版告诉我们，“颇为出人意料”，《村庄》“引起了农业科学家、发展研究学生和华盛顿政策制定者的认真注意”。
1988年，克里奇菲尔德第一本关于农民的书《金碗被打破：四种文化中的农民生活》由一家大学出版社再版，作为“推荐用于课程”的教材。
克里奇菲尔德在埃及的研究由福特基金会资助（他后来还获得洛克菲勒基金会和其他基金会的资助，并受雇于美国国际开发署，担任第三世界村庄事务顾问）。换言之，他对农民的“现实主义”描绘，得到了一大批评论者、编辑、出版者、发展专家、政策制定者、资助委员会成员和大学教师的支持。

en: In December 1981, not long after the publication of Shahhat and immediately following the appearance of Villages, Critchfield was named as one of the first half dozen recipients of the new MacArthur Foundation fellowships, a $250,000 award nominated secretly by unnamed scholars and given annually to individuals whose work is of outstanding intelligence and originality. Besides “the peasant,” and the Middle Eastern peasant in particular, is there any stereotype in the Orientalist portrayal of the non-West whose racism and ahistoricism could remain so acceptable that the author of its latest incarnation might find his work so well received and rewarded?
zh: 1981年12月，在《沙哈特》出版后不久、紧接着《村庄》问世之后，克里奇菲尔德成为新设立的麦克阿瑟基金会奖学金首批六名获得者之一。这项奖金为25万美元，由不具名的学者秘密提名，每年授予作品具有非凡才智和原创性的人。除了“农民”，尤其是中东农民之外，东方主义对非西方的描绘中还有哪种刻板印象，其种族主义和非历史性能够如此被接受，以致其最新化身的作者会发觉自己的作品受到如此热情的欢迎和奖励？

en: postscript
zh: 后记

en: This chapter was first published as an article in the International Journal of Middle East Studies. Following its publication I was contacted by the sisters of Henry Habib Ayrout and indirectly by Richard Critchfield. These contacts led to further discoveries and opened additional questions.
zh: 本章最初作为一篇文章发表于《国际中东研究杂志》。文章发表后，亨利·哈比卜·艾鲁特的姐妹们联系了我，理查德·克里奇菲尔德也间接与我联系。这些接触带来了进一步的发现，也引出了更多问题。

en: The reader may be little surprised to learn that Father Ayrout wrote his classic study of the Egyptian peasant without any firsthand knowledge of rural Egypt. He had grown up in Cairo and left Egypt secretly in 1926 at the age of eighteen, against the wishes of his father, who intended him to follow his two other sons into the father’s profession of architecture. Dressed in a cassock and carrying a passport supplied by the French Jesuits, at whose school he had studied in Cairo, Ayrout left for twelve years of training at a Jesuit college in Lyon. He completed his study of the Egyptian peasant as a dissertation ten years later, relying on books such as Winifred Blackman’s The Fellahin of Upper Egypt and on correspondence with former school friends in Cairo whose fathers owned large agricultural estates. He himself never visited rural Egypt while writing the book, and had probably seen no more of the countryside than the view from the train on his way to Alexandria.
zh: 读者得知艾鲁特神父在写他那部关于埃及农民的经典研究时，对埃及乡村没有任何亲身了解，或许不太会感到惊讶。他在开罗长大，1926年十八岁时违背父亲的意愿秘密离开埃及；父亲本打算让他像两个哥哥一样从事父亲的建筑行业。艾鲁特身穿神父长袍，带着法国耶稣会提供的护照——他曾在开罗的耶稣会学校就读——前往里昂，在一所耶稣会学院接受十二年训练。十年后，他以关于埃及农民的研究作为学位论文完成学业；写作时依赖温妮弗雷德·布莱克曼的《上埃及的费拉欣》等著作，以及与开罗旧日同窗的通信——这些人的父亲拥有大型农业庄园。写这本书时，他本人从未访问过埃及乡村，关于乡下他所见到的，大概也仅限于前往亚历山大途中从火车上看到的景象。

en: Ayrout returned to Egypt in 1941. The German army had occupied Lyon, leaving the Jesuit schools in Egypt and the Levant deprived of funds from France and forced to reduce their operations or close down. With no conventional Jesuit employment available, Ayrout began his educational and missionary work in Upper Egypt, eventually founding more than a hundred schools among the Coptic community and becoming the resident authority on rural Egypt for foreign scholars and journalists.

“Anyone coming to Egypt to study the fellaheen, the peasants,” wrote Jay Walz, the New York Times correspondent in Cairo from 1959 to 1964, “sooner or later called on the dynamic, bristly-haired Jesuit priest.”

In 1968 the Ford Foundation decided to tap Ayrout’s expertise, commissioning him to spend seven months touring villages in East Africa and then flying him to New York to give eight lectures at Columbia University on rural development. On reaching New York in April 1969, he suffered a heart attack and died.
zh: 艾鲁特于1941年返回埃及。德国军队占领了里昂，使埃及和黎凡特的耶稣会学校失去来自法国的资金，被迫缩减业务或关闭。由于没有常规的耶稣会职务可做，艾鲁特开始在上埃及从事教育和传教工作，最终在科普特社群中创办了一百多所学校，并成为外国学者和记者眼中埃及乡村问题的常驻权威。
“任何到埃及来研究费拉欣、研究农民的人，”1959年至1964年担任《纽约时报》驻开罗记者的杰伊·沃尔兹写道，“迟早都会拜访这位精力充沛、头发硬直竖立的耶稣会神父。”
1968年，福特基金会决定借助艾鲁特的专门知识，委托他花七个月时间考察东非的村庄，随后又请他飞往纽约，在哥伦比亚大学就乡村发展作八场讲座。1969年4月抵达纽约时，他突发心脏病去世。

en: Ayrout’s sister, Janette De Bono-Ayrout, who graciously invited me to her apartment in Cairo, did not believe the work of Gustave Le Bon was ever read by her brother or his circle, as she had never heard the name mentioned. After tea, she invited me to see the personal library of her late husband, the Egyptian historian Jacques Tagher. She was gently surprised when we found on the shelves a two-volume edition of Le Bon’s L’Homme et la Société.
zh: 艾鲁特的妹妹雅内特·德·博诺-艾鲁特亲切地邀请我到她开罗的公寓；她不相信她哥哥或其圈子读过古斯塔夫·勒邦的著作，因为她从未听人提起这个名字。喝过茶后，她请我参观她已故丈夫、埃及历史学家雅克·塔盖尔的私人藏书。当我们在书架上发现一部两卷本的勒邦《人与社会》时，她微微感到惊讶。

en: Richard Critchfield acknowledged in a published response to my essay that he had “paraphrased”Ayrout. Busy with further studies of peasants in Mindanao and Java, however, he had forgotten to add the references when copyediting Shahhat. He promised to add them to a future edition.

I pointed out in reply that he would need not just references but quotation marks, since many of his borrowings from Ayrout were verbatim;that he would also have to do the same with passages copied from other authors not mentioned in my essay, such as the nineteenth-century Orientalist Edward William Lane, which may have been more numerous than those copied from Ayrout (even the description of Shahhat’s house, for example, including its architectural details, comes almost word-for-word from the account of “dwellings of the lower orders” in Lane’s famous 1835 study, The Manners and Customs of the Modern Egyptians); and finally, that he would have to explain to the reader why his description of Shahhat’s house comes from a book written a hundred years before it was built and the portrait of Shahhat’s visit to the market, his work in the fields, his character, and his facial appearance were taken from an account written almost a generation before he was born.
zh: 理查德·克里奇菲尔德在发表的一篇对我文章的回应中承认，他“改写”了艾鲁特。然而，由于忙于研究棉兰老岛和爪哇的农民，他在编辑《沙哈特》时忘了添上参考文献。他承诺在未来的版本中补上。

我在答复中指出，他不仅需要参考文献，还需要引号，因为他从艾鲁特那里借用的许多内容都是逐字照搬；他还必须对从我这篇文章未提及的其他作者那里抄来的段落做同样处理，例如19世纪东方学家爱德华·威廉·莱恩，其被抄段落可能比抄自艾鲁特的还多（例如，甚至对沙哈特房屋的描写，包括其建筑细节，也几乎逐字出自莱恩1835年名著《现代埃及人的风俗与习惯》中关于“下层阶级住所”的记述）；最后，他还必须向读者解释，为什么他对沙哈特房屋的描写来自一本在该房建成一百年前写成的书，而沙哈特去市场、田间劳作、性格和面部外貌的肖像，则取自一份几乎在他出生一代人之前写成的记述。

en: I wrote the original essay without visiting the village of Buʿairat, for the improbability of Critchfield’s account was clear enough from its ignorance of recent history and its stereotypical image of an unchanging village life. I subsequently visited the village several times, however, and found the book’s portrait even more bizarre than I had suspected. Critchfield suggested that the location of Shahhat’s hamlet within Buʿairat, adjacent to Medinet Habu, the ruined temple of Ramases III, indicated that this was a particularly ancient community and had preserved more Pharaonic practices than most. In fact, while the main village a mile to the south was probably the result of an Arab settlement (on an ancient site) within the previous three hundred years, Shahhat’s hamlet was built within the preceding fifty years.

Most of the families that settled there came to serve the needs of modern archaeology and tourism. Shahhat’s great-grandfather Khalifa is said to have moved to the area from Karnak across the Nile, possibly when the French-run government antiquities service for which he worked began excavations nearby. In the 1880s he served as a guide and assistant for an American archaeologist and antiquities collector, Charles Wilbour.

Together with another family, who also worked for the antiquities service, Khalifa’s descendants built most of the hamlet. Many of Shahhat’s uncles and cousins continued to work for French archaeologists, others for Americans from the University of Chicago, who had begun excavations at Medinet Habu in the 1920s. Three of the uncles invested their income in the building of small hotels. Shahhat’s father was less successful. He became the local supplier of alcohol to the foreign archaeological missions, and died of his alcoholism. Shahhat himself, although happy to hoe a field when a tourist turned up to videotape the character from Critchfield’s book, had to spend most winters elsewhere in Egypt as a foreman and labor contractor on French archaeological digs—and struggled himself against his father’s illness.
zh: 我最初写那篇文章时没有访问布艾拉特村，因为克里奇菲尔德的记述对近代历史一无所知，对一成不变的乡村生活持刻板印象，这已足以说明它不可信。然而，我后来多次访问该村，发现书中的画像比我猜想的还要离奇。克里奇菲尔德暗示，沙哈特的小村在布艾拉特内的位置，紧邻拉美西斯三世的神庙废墟美迪内特哈布，表明这是一个特别古老的共同体，比大多数村落保存了更多的法老习俗。事实上，南面一英里外的主村可能是在此前三百年内（在一个古代遗址上）由阿拉伯人定居形成的，而沙哈特的小村则是在此前五十年内建成的。
在此定居的家庭大多是为满足现代考古和旅游的需要而来的。据说沙哈特的曾祖父哈利法从尼罗河对岸的卡纳克迁到此地，可能是在他供职的法国人管理的政府文物局开始在附近发掘的时候。1880年代，他曾为美国考古学家和文物收藏家查尔斯·威尔伯担任向导和助手。

哈利法的后代与另一个同样在文物局工作的家庭一起，建起了这座小村的大部分。沙哈特的许多叔伯和堂表亲继续为法国考古学家工作，其他人则为芝加哥大学的美国人工作——后者在1920年代开始发掘美迪内特哈布。三位叔伯把收入投资于修建小旅馆。沙哈特的父亲则不那么成功。他成为当地向外国考古队供应酒类的人，并死于酗酒。沙哈特本人虽然乐于在游客前来拍摄克里奇菲尔德书中人物时去锄一块地，但大多数冬天都不得不在埃及其他地方度过，在法国考古队中当工头和劳务承包商——他自己也一直在与父亲的疾病作斗争。

en: This long history of relations between local families, foreign archaeology, and a small-scale tourist industry, mixed in with the agrarian economy of sugarcane and household farming, has formed the complex reality of Shahhat’s village. We cannot read Critchfield’s work as a portrait of this reality, for the book deliberately ignores the relations between locals and outsiders that have formed it. We should see the book, at best, as one more aspect of those relations.
zh: 当地家庭、外国考古业和小规模旅游业之间的这段悠久关系史，与甘蔗和家庭农作构成的农业经济交织在一起，形成了沙哈特村庄的复杂现实。我们不能把克里奇菲尔德的著作读作这一现实的画像，因为该书有意忽视了塑造这一现实的当地人与外来者之间的关系。充其量，我们应当把这本书看作这些关系中的又一个方面。

en: Richard Critchfield died on December 10, 1994, in Washington, D.C. He had gone there to attend a publication party for his tenth book, The Villagers, in which he retold stories from the dozen or more villages he had described in his earlier works.

His obituary in the New York Times mentioned that he was survived by an elder brother, James Critchfield, of Delaplane, Virginia. James Critchfield, I subsequently discovered, worked for the United States Central Intelligence Agency. The discovery led to further questions about the production of Critchfield’s portraits of the Third World peasant.
zh: 理查德·克里奇菲尔德于1994年12月10日在华盛顿特区去世。他去那里是为了参加自己第十本书《村民》的出版聚会；他在书中重述了此前著作中描述过的十几个村庄的故事。
《纽约时报》的讣告提到，他的遗属中有一位住在弗吉尼亚州德拉普兰的哥哥詹姆斯·克里奇菲尔德。我后来发现，詹姆斯·克里奇菲尔德曾在美国中央情报局工作。这一发现引出了更多问题：克里奇菲尔德那些第三世界农民画像究竟是如何生产出来的？

en: James Critchfield belonged to the founding generation of the CIA.After working closely with former Nazi intelligence officers in postwar Germany, he was appointed the first director of CIA clandestine operations in the Near East in 1959, and went on to become a senior architect of U.S. policy in the Middle East for three decades.

One of his first actions, in February 1960, according to a later Congressional investigation, was an attempt to murder the president of Iraq, General ʿAbd al-Karim Qasim. Critchfield’s idea was to have the president killed with a poisoned handkerchief prepared by the CIA’s Technical Services Division. (The attempt failed, but Qasim was killed three years later in a coup welcomed and possibly aided by the CIA, which brought to power the Baʿth, the party of Saddam Hussein.)

The attempted murder of Qasim was one of the actions for which James Critchfield’s supervisor, Richard Helms, the director of Central Intelligence from 1966 to 1973, was mildly sanctioned by the U.S. Senate in 1977, for allowing the CIA to function as though it had “a licence to operate freely outside the dictates of the law.”
zh: 詹姆斯·克里奇菲尔德属于中情局的创始一代。战后在德国与前纳粹情报官员密切合作之后，他于1959年被任命为中情局近东秘密行动的首任主任，随后又在三十年间成为美国中东政策的高级设计者之一。
据后来的一项国会调查，他在1960年2月最早采取的行动之一，是试图谋杀伊拉克总统阿卜杜勒·卡里姆·卡塞姆将军。克里奇菲尔德的设想是用中情局技术服务处准备的一块毒手帕把总统杀死。（这次行动失败了，但卡塞姆三年后在一场中情局乐见、可能还提供了协助的政变中被杀，那场政变使萨达姆·侯赛因的复兴党上台。）
谋杀卡塞姆未遂事件，是詹姆斯·克里奇菲尔德的上级、1966年至1973年任中央情报总监的理查德·赫尔姆斯于1977年在美国参议院受到轻微处分的行动之一，原因是他允许中情局像“拥有在法律规定之外自由行动的许可证”那样运作。

en: One cannot assume without further evidence that Richard Critchfield worked in the same profession as his brother. However, he certainly moved in the same circles. The Villagers, his last book, acknowledged the “advice, suggestions, help and hospitality” he received from Cynthia Helms, the wife of his brother’s former supervisor; from Robert S. McNamara, the former U.S. secretary of defense; and from a number of other figures associated with the CIA and the politico-military establishment. These were unusually well placed associates for a man who insisted in each of his books that he was just a journalist who wrote about peasants in obscure parts of the world.
zh: 没有更多证据，不能假定理查德·克里奇菲尔德与他哥哥从事同一职业。然而，他肯定出入于同一个圈子。他的最后一本书《村民》感谢了从他哥哥前上司的妻子辛西娅·赫尔姆斯、美国前国防部长罗伯特·S. 麦克纳马拉，以及若干与中情局和政军体制有关联的其他人物那里得到的“建议、提议、帮助和款待”。对于一个在每本书中都坚称自己只是报道世界偏远地区农民的记者的人来说，这些交往对象的地位高得不寻常。

en: One might also notice the way his choice of villages, always portrayed as out-of-the-way places, followed the changing focus of U.S. imperial concerns, some of them at the time quite secretive. He was in India and Nepal in 1959–62, the years coinciding with probably the largest CIA operation of the time: a secret program based in Nepal to train and arm Tibetan refugees to fight the Chinese occupation in Tibet.

Critchfield’s visits to Nepal were spaced between spells teaching journalism at the university in Nagpur, the birthplace and headquarters of the rising Hindu fascist movement. By the mid-1960s, an account of the CIA program in Nepal reports, “CIA officer James Critchfield described the guerrillas’ achievements inside Tibet as ‘minimal.’ . . . In any case, the CIA’s attention was shifting to Indochina.”

Richard Critchfield followed suit, arriving in Vietnam in 1964 as a reporter for the Washington Star and writing the book that promoted the views of British military intelligence, which the CIA was then urging Washington to adopt. From Vietnam he took trips to Java, then spent a year there in 1966–67, just after the CIA had helped the Suharto regime seize power and carry out the killing of as many as a million political opponents. He also spent a year in Washington as a White House correspondent for the Star, which had its own connections with the CIA.
zh: 人们还可以注意到，他对村庄的选择——这些村庄总被描绘成偏僻之地——如何跟随美国帝国关切焦点的变化，其中一些在当时相当隐秘。1959年至1962年，他在印度和尼泊尔，那几年恰好与当时大概是中情局最大规模的一次行动同时：一项以尼泊尔为基地的秘密计划，训练和武装西藏难民，以对抗中国对西藏的占领。
克里奇菲尔德对尼泊尔的访问，穿插在他于那格浦尔大学讲授新闻学的几段时间之间；那格浦尔是正在兴起的印度教法西斯运动的发源地和总部。到1960年代中期，一份关于中情局尼泊尔计划的记述报告说，“中情局官员詹姆斯·克里奇菲尔德把游击队在西藏境内的成绩描述为‘极小’……无论如何，中情局的注意力正在转向印度支那。”
理查德·克里奇菲尔德也随之而行，1964年作为《华盛顿星报》记者抵达越南，并写出那本宣扬英国军事情报观点的书，而中情局当时正敦促华盛顿采纳这种观点。他从越南前往爪哇，随后于1966年至1967年在那里待了一年，恰好在中情局帮助苏哈托政权夺取权力、杀害多达一百万政治反对者之后不久。他还在华盛顿担任《星报》的白宫记者一年；该报本身与中情局有联系。

en: In 1969 Critchfield abandoned the Star to become a full-time “reporter from villages,” with a grant from the Alicia Patterson Fund.

For his first long stay in a single village he chose the seemingly out-of-the-way island of Mauritius, in the southern Indian Ocean. The Indian Ocean, however, was then at the center of another U.S. military expansion. Mauritius had just acquired its independence from Britain and was offering naval facilities to the Soviet Union. The United States was building its own Indian Ocean naval and intelligence base on the island of Diego Garcia, previously attached to Mauritius but retained by Britain and leased to the United States. To ensure the secrecy of the new base, Critchfield’s friend McNamara demanded that the entire population of the archipelago to which Diego Garcia belonged, the Chagos Islands, be removed. Britain agreed to secretly round up the inhabitants, against their will and in violation of international law, and ship them to Mauritius. As Critchfield arrived on the island, Britain and the United States were paying the Mauritian government £650,000 to help settle the Chagos Islanders, in the hope that news of their illegal deportation would not reach the West.
zh: 1969年，克里奇菲尔德放弃《星报》，在艾丽西亚·帕特森基金的资助下成为专职“村庄报道人”。

他首次在一个村庄长期居留，选择了南印度洋看似偏僻的毛里求斯岛。然而，印度洋当时正处于又一次美国军事扩张的中心。毛里求斯刚刚脱离英国获得独立，并向苏联提供海军设施。美国正在迭戈加西亚岛上修建自己的印度洋海军和情报基地；该岛原先隶属于毛里求斯，但被英国保留并租给美国。为确保新基地的保密，克里奇菲尔德的朋友麦克纳马拉要求把迭戈加西亚所属群岛——查戈斯群岛——的全部人口迁走。英国同意秘密围捕居民，违背其意愿并违反国际法，用船把他们运到毛里求斯。克里奇菲尔德抵达该岛时，英国和美国正向毛里求斯政府支付65万英镑，帮助安置查戈斯岛民，希望他们被非法驱逐的消息不会传到西方。

en: Building the base on Diego Garcia was part of an expansion of U.S. power in the Gulf and the eastern Mediterranean, an expansion that involved new relations with the two leading non-Western military powers in the region, Iran and Egypt. Critchfield’s village studies over the ensuing years followed these shifting concerns. He lived in a village on the border between Iran and Iraq in 1971, just as his brother had helped persuade President Nixon to start building Iran into a heavily armed ally of the United States and begin secretly destabilizing the Baʿthist government in Iraq. In 1974 he arrived in Egypt, within weeks of Washington reestablishing diplomatic ties with Cairo. Although most of rural Egypt was still offlimits to visiting Westerners, by choosing a village on the edge of the tourist area near Luxor Critchfield was able to spend time in the Egyptian countryside during this critical period of renewed U.S. involvement in the country.
zh: 在迭戈加西亚修建基地，是美国在波斯湾和东地中海扩张实力的一部分；这场扩张涉及与该地区两个主要非西方军事大国——伊朗和埃及——建立新关系。克里奇菲尔德此后几年的村庄研究跟随着这些变化的关切。1971年，他住在伊朗与伊拉克边境的一个村庄；恰在此时，他哥哥帮助说服尼克松总统开始把伊朗打造成美国的重武装盟友，并着手秘密破坏伊拉克复兴党政府的稳定。1974年，他抵达埃及，距华盛顿与开罗重新建立外交关系仅数周。尽管埃及大部分乡村当时仍禁止西方访客进入，克里奇菲尔德通过选择卢克索附近旅游区边缘的一个村庄，得以在美国重新介入该国的这一关键时期在埃及乡村逗留。

en: So was Critchfield an American spy? I do not know and do not think this is the interesting question. A few years after Critchfield’s book appeared a leading Egyptian journal published a series of articles warning about the “penetration” of Egypt by American scholars and development experts, whose research posed a threat to the country’s “national security.”

One article reported the views of the sociologist Saʿd Eddin Ibrahim, who gave the example of an American study that had collected data on local leadership in four hundred Egyptian villages, warning that such information could be used in ways detrimental to Egypt.

This seems unlikely. Given the evidence of Critchfield’s writings, it is hard to imagine him gathering anything in the way of useful information, just as there is very little one could learn from a survey of “leadership” in four hundred, or even forty, Egyptian villages. As I explain in later chapters, it would be difficult to point to any American research on Egyptian rural development that gathered information reliable enough to threaten the country’s security. If there was any threat it lay in the danger of invoking the shibboleth of “national security,” an invocation aiding those forces of repression for whom this is always a useful term. Saʿd Eddin Ibrahim himself became a victim of this repression when he was sentenced a decade later to seven years in prison for alleged activities threatening national security.
zh: 那么，克里奇菲尔德是美国间谍吗？我不知道，也不认为这是有趣的问题。克里奇菲尔德的书出版几年后，埃及一家主要期刊发表了一系列文章，警告美国学者和发展专家对埃及的“渗透”，称他们的研究对该国的“国家安全”构成威胁。
一篇文章报道了社会学家萨阿德·埃丁·易卜拉欣的观点，他以一项收集了埃及四百个村庄地方领导层数据的美国研究为例，警告这类信息可能被用于损害埃及。

这似乎不大可能。从克里奇菲尔德著述中的证据看，很难想象他能收集到什么有用的信息，正如从对埃及四百个、甚至四十个村庄“领导层”的调查中，人们也学不到多少东西。正如我在后面几章所解释的，很难指出有哪项关于埃及乡村发展的美国研究收集了可靠到足以威胁该国安全的信息。如果说存在任何威胁，那也在于援引“国家安全”这一咒语的危险；这种援引会帮助那些镇压势力，对他们而言，这个说法始终有用。萨阿德·埃丁·易卜拉欣本人后来也成了这种镇压的受害者：十年后，他因被指控从事威胁国家安全的活动而被判处七年监禁。

en: The importance of Critchfield’s connections with America’s “national security” regime, whether direct or indirect, lies elsewhere, in unraveling the political genealogy of such expertise on the Middle East, and on the question of “the peasant” in particular. Only recently has it been understood how pervasively the CIA influenced the production of academic and intellectual culture around the world in the second half of the twentieth century. The story of the Congress for Cultural Freedom, established by the CIA in Paris, is now well known, including its funding of the British magazine Encounter. The CIA’s efforts extended well beyond this, to include the funding of art exhibits, in particular those promoting abstract expressionism; concerts featuring the work of avant-garde American composers; academic and cultural congresses; and books, translations, and a wide variety of journals willing to criticize Marxism or the Soviet Union and to support, or at least remain silent on, American violence in Vietnam and other parts of the world.

Among the journals the agency funded overseas was an Arab counterpart to Encounter magazine, al-Hiwar, established in Beirut in 1962 under the editorship of a distinguished Palestinian writer, Tawfiq Sayyigh.
Al-Hiwar ceased publication in 1967 after the CIA funding of the Congress for Cultural Freedom was revealed.
zh: 克里奇菲尔德与美国“国家安全”体制的联系，无论是直接还是间接，其重要性在别处：在于揭示这类中东专门知识、尤其是关于“农民”问题的专门知识的政治谱系。直到最近，人们才认识到中情局对20世纪下半叶世界各地学术和知识文化的生产影响之广泛。中情局在巴黎创立的文化自由大会的故事如今已广为人知，包括它资助英国杂志《交锋》。中情局的行动远不止于此，还包括资助艺术展览，特别是推广抽象表现主义的展览；举办美国先锋派作曲家作品音乐会；资助学术和文化会议；以及资助书籍、翻译和各种愿意批评马克思主义或苏联、支持（或至少对美国在越南和世界其他地方的暴力保持沉默）的期刊。
该机构在海外资助的期刊中，有一份相当于《交锋》的阿拉伯语刊物《对话》（al-Hiwar），1962年创办于贝鲁特，由杰出的巴勒斯坦作家陶菲克·萨伊格主编。
在中情局资助文化自由大会一事曝光后，《对话》于1967年停刊。

en: These connections with the clandestine U.S. production of cultural and academic expertise may have extended not only to work like Critchfield’s, but also to the U.S. publication of Ayrout’s Egyptian Peasant. The book was published in the United States, as I noted, a quarter of a century after it was first written, but coinciding with a renewed American interest in domestic Egyptian affairs. Its publication was arranged by Morroe Berger, who had played a role in the creation of the National Defense Education Act in 1958 and, as I mentioned earlier, was the first chair of the Near and Middle East Committee of the Social Science Research Council and the founding president of the Middle East Studies Association of North America. As a student in New York in the late 1930s, Berger had been a member of the New York Trotskyist movement, with others like Irving Howe, Seymour Martin Lipset, and Gertrude Himmelfarb, many of whom became active anticommunists after the war and in several cases moved far to the right.

Some of them, including the journalist Irving Kristol, the N.Y.U. philosopher Sidney Hook, and the editor of Encounter, Melvin Lasky, were later funded and promoted by the CIA. Like many other scholars who came to area studies after World War II, Berger had worked in intelligence during the war, and he, too, had connections with the CIA. He was a member of the Congress for Cultural Freedom and was the scholar who recruited the editor for the Arab counterpart to Encounter magazine, al-Hiwar. The generous amount of CIA money that he offered the prospective editor carried with it one stipulation: that the journal publish articles dealing with the unfavorable position of Muslim communities in the Soviet Union.
zh: 这些与美国秘密生产文化和学术专门知识的联系，可能不仅延伸到克里奇菲尔德这样的作品，也延伸到艾鲁特《埃及农民》在美国的出版。如我所述，这本书在首次写成四分之一世纪之后才在美国出版，但恰逢美国重新关注埃及国内事务。该书的出版由莫罗·伯杰安排；他曾参与1958年《国防教育法》的制定，并且如前所述，是社会研究理事会近东与中东委员会的首任主席和北美中东研究协会的创会主席。1930年代末在纽约求学时，伯杰曾是纽约托洛茨基主义运动的成员，同侪还有欧文·豪、西摩·马丁·利普塞特和格特鲁德·希梅尔法布等人；他们中的许多人在战后成为积极的反共分子，有几位还远远转向了右翼。
其中一些人，包括记者欧文·克里斯托尔、纽约大学哲学家悉尼·胡克和《交锋》主编梅尔文·拉斯基，后来得到中情局的资助和提携。像二战后投身区域研究的许多其他学者一样，伯杰在战争期间从事过情报工作，他也与中情局有联系。他是文化自由大会的成员，也是为《交锋》的阿拉伯语对应刊物《对话》招募主编的学者。他向这位拟任主编提供的大笔中情局资金附带一项条件：该刊必须发表讨论苏联境内穆斯林群体不利处境的文章。

en: The most serious questions raised by this story are neither Critchfield’s plagiarisms of Ayrout, nor the possible connections with the activities of U.S. intelligence work and the clandestine political funding of American journalism and scholarship. The most important issue is the structure of academic expertise that enabled these forms of prejudice, ignorance, and misrepresentation to flourish and gave such dubious books their circulation and acceptance.
zh: 这个故事所提出的最严肃问题，既不是克里奇菲尔德对艾鲁特的抄袭，也不是与美国情报活动、以及对美国新闻业和学术界的秘密政治资助之间可能存在的联系。最重要的问题，是那种使这些偏见、无知和歪曲得以滋长、并使如此可疑的书得以流通和被接受的学术专门知识结构。

en: There was also an active debate on these issues in the press. In al-Ahram on Feb. 17, 18, and 19, 1937, for example, Bint al-Shatiʾ (the pseudonym of ʿAʾisha ʿAbd al-Rahman), the author of al-Rif al-misri (Rural Egypt) (Cairo: Maktabat al-Wafd, 1936), described the evils of the cotton processing industry, explaining how twenty-five thousand children aged eight to fifteen were employed that year loading and unloading the ginning machines in cotton ginning and pressing factories, working amid stifling dust from 5 A.M. to 9 P.M. each day without a break (Ayrout, The Fellaheen, 63). The various Cairo editions of Ayrout also continued the debate. The French edition of 1943 had a preface by Fuʾad Abaza Pasha. The English-language edition published in Cairo in 1945 had a foreword by Muhammad Taher Pasha, a prominent landowner and businessman who was a member of the royal family and a member of parliament. Tahir praised Ayrout’s “objectivity,” and warned that at this “turning-point of its history” the country needed “a complete and intimate collaboration among all classes” based on “a particularly sympathetic understanding . . . of their peasantry by the upper class and landowners” (Ayrout, The Fellaheen, 5). On Tahir, see Eric Davis, Challenging Colonialism: Bank Misr and Egyptian Industrialization, 1920–1941 (Princeton, N.J.: Princeton University Press, 1983), 141.
zh: 在这些问题上，报刊上也有激烈的辩论。例如，1937年2月17、18、19日的《金字塔报》上，《埃及乡村》（al-Rif al-misri，开罗：Maktabat al-Wafd, 1936）的作者宾特·沙提（Bint al-Shatiʾ，即阿伊莎·阿卜杜勒·拉赫曼的笔名）描述了棉花加工业的祸害，说明当年有2.5万名八至十五岁的儿童受雇在轧棉和压棉厂装卸轧棉机，每天从清晨5点到晚上9点在令人窒息的粉尘中工作，没有休息（Ayrout, The Fellaheen, 63）。艾鲁特著作的各种开罗版本也延续了这场辩论。1943年的法文版有福阿德·阿巴扎帕夏的序言。1945年在开罗出版的英文版有穆罕默德·塔希尔帕夏的序言；他是一位显赫的地主和商人，也是王室成员和国会议员。塔希尔赞扬艾鲁特的“客观性”，并警告说，在这个“历史转折点”，国家需要“所有阶级之间全面而密切的合作”，其基础是“上层阶级和地主对农民的特别同情的理解”（Ayrout, The Fellaheen, 5）。关于塔希尔，见 Eric Davis, Challenging Colonialism: Bank Misr and Egyptian Industrialization, 1920–1941 (Princeton, N.J.: Princeton University Press, 1983), 141.

en: When Mirrit Butrus Ghali stopped opposing land reform and published a proposal in 1945 to halt the accumulation of land by large estates (to affect only future land purchases, not existing or inherited holdings), he argued for a limit of one hundred acres rather than fifty on the grounds that the lower limit would “restrict the initiative of the rural middle class, those rural notables who, in our opinion, have the vital task of infusing life into rural society.” Quoted in Gabriel Baer, A History of Landownership in Modern Egypt, 1800–1950 (Oxford: Oxford University Press, 1962), 212.

en: Ayrout’s claim, echoing Le Bon, that the Egyptian village “is not a community in the social sense, not an organism, but a mass” was the main evidence used by Gabriel Baer, an Israeli scholar who for a generation became a leading authority on the modern history of rural Egypt, to argue that by the nineteenth century the Egyptian village no longer existed as a corporate community. “The Dissolution of the Egyptian Village Community,” in Studies in the Social History of Modern Egypt (Chicago: University of Chicago Press, 1969), 17–29. en: When the villagers have had enough of all the violence, there remains the possibility of kayf, “a word of profound significance” according to Ayrout. He says it denotes “a kind of wakeful passivity which means doing nothing, saying nothing, thinking nothing” (136). Critchfield explains that “in Egypt there is a mental state called kaif, when a man does nothing, says nothing, and thinks nothing. It is a kind of wakeful passivity” (183).
zh: 当村民受够了所有这些暴力时，还有凯夫（kayf）这一可能，用艾鲁特的话说，这是“一个意义深远的词”。他说，它指的是“一种清醒的被动状态，意味着什么也不做、什么也不说、什么也不想”（136）。克里奇菲尔德解释说，“在埃及，有一种精神状态叫作 kaif，此时人什么也不做、什么也不说、什么也不想。它是一种清醒的被动状态”（183）。

en: Al-Ahram al-iqtisadi, Oct. 4, 1982. The series of articles was published in al-Ahram al-iqtisadi in October and November 1982. Several important criticisms were made in these and other articles, drawing attention to the way Egyptian scholars and scientific centers had been co-opted into consultancy work or joint research projects under American auspices, in which the goals, methods, and assumptions of the analysis were determined by the agenda of American development policy, and pointing out how the bulk of the fees and the credit for such joint research were earned by the Americans, even in the frequent cases in which most of the research was done by Egyptians and the foreigner did little more than correct the English of the final draft. However, some authors also called for the Egyptian state to become more directly involved in the control and direction of research, for CAPMAS (the Central Agency for Public Mobilization and Statistics) to reassert its power to license all research projects in the country, and even for the prosecutor general and the state security services to enforce more strictly a 1960 law providing six-month prison sentences for those disclosing state information on national planning, food consumption, and trade (al-Ahram al-iqtisadi, Nov. 8, 1982).

en: Personal communication from Ibrahim Abu-Lughod, Aug. 3, 2000. Berger had attempted to recruit Abu-Lughod to edit the magazine. Berger did not reveal the source of the funds, but the amount of money on offer and the stipulation concerning the Soviet Union made Abu-Lughod immediately suspicious. When the facts about their involvement with the CIA emerged in the late 1960s, many of the American intellectuals who received funds from the CIA claimed that they had not realized who was paying them. Saunders, The Cultural Cold War, effectively refutes the claim.
